OWNERSHIP
- Each new package (for example AUD, VID, or one MEDIA/CODEC package) is src/<pkg>/{__init__,api,levers}.py with ONE LeverSet whose PREFIX generates the env names PREFIX_FIELD (O3). Only spine/lever.py reads os.environ (O1). Only the spine calls from_env (O8), and the runtime latch closes assembly after build().
- It must be registered in five places, and three tests compare them:
  - spine/assemble.py:166 PACKAGES
  - spine/compose.py:114 APIS
  - spine/loop.py:355 _PKG_DIR
  - tests/test_contract.py:88 PKG_DIR (K1 checks that it agrees with APIS)
  - the census and contract documents
- A package may import only stdlib, torch and spine.{lever, units, derive, rng, wire, gate, init} (tests/test_ownership.py:2315 ALLOWED_SPINE; O10 is an allowlist; K3).
- It may not import LM, TOK, WORLD or DATA. Anything it needs from them (LM.width, LM.vocab_slots, obs_emb, the head callable, a codec encoder) arrives as a keyword argument the composition root passes. Example of the idiom: open_store(key_dim=LM.width, vocab_slots=LM.vocab_slots) at compose.py:2439.
- Every lever needs a census row. tests/test_census.py:293 N2 fails for a lever with no census ancestor unless it has a DEPARTURES entry or an "(amendment: NAME)" row in .rework/census.json, which is how OPT_GRAD_CLIP and MEM_JUDGE_FRAC landed.
- Every lever must be named in some entry point's `LEVERS READ:` line (K4, contract §0). A lever must be declared with a unit from spine/units.py and a literal default (O2), and help text is rendered into docs/05_DEFAULTS.md. That file is generated, and A10 fails until `python3 tools/render_defaults.py` is re-run.
- Frozen Configs: a Config cannot change after build().

WIRES VERSUS ARGUMENTS
- A d_ wire is a build-time function of frozen lever values only (spine/assemble.py COUPLINGS :717, with the compute allowlist at :207). The budget is 19 of 25 cross-package wires spent (spine/wire.py:54 WIRE_BUDGET=25; docs/03_WIRING.md), so six remain. Intra-package wires cost nothing.
- Anything MEASURED is refused as a wire: codec bits per frame, measured tokens per second, the real media share of a window. Precedent: SIG.d_signature_width_bytes is in NOT_WIRES (assemble.py:1202) because bytes_per_token is measured. Those values must be derive-and-keep through a named join in compose.py, like _signature_width.
- Plausible legitimate wires:
  - CODEC.codebook_size x n_codebooks -> TOK/LM reserved-range size. This is IRREDUCIBLE, since the model's rows must hold the codebook.
  - CODEC.frames_per_window -> WORLD horizon bounds. This is only a wire if it is declared rather than measured.
- Every wire needs a written `why`, which O6 checks, and docs/03_WIRING.md must be regenerated (`python3 tools/render_wiring.py`; A9 fails if stale).
- Per-flush tensors (media embeddings, forecasts) are runtime ARGUMENTS in a LOOP_ORDER row, never wires. world/api.py:542's docstring states this for forecast.

CLOCK KINDS
- spine/units.py has Steps, Flushes, Windows, Backwards, Epochs and Selections (:324-360). Comparing across kinds raises UnitError. A new kind (Frames, Samples, or modality windows) must be declared IN units.py and added to CLOCK_KINDS (:382). _verify_kind refuses kinds declared elsewhere.
- Any cross-kind conversion must be a named function in spine/derive.py with a known-answer table in tests/test_derive.py.
- Every cadence goes through Cadences.due(key, period, clock) with a period from a typed accessor that returns a Clock. Examples: EVAL.curve_period, DOM.manage_period. K9 refuses a bare lever read. compose.py:_periods (:3512) holds the keys.
- Proposal 01 (docs/proposals/01_MODALITIES.md:91-110) asks for the M1 decision, one Windows kind versus split kinds, BEFORE any encoder is written.

CHECKPOINT AND GEOMETRY
- Every piece of state needs:
  - a save path: <pkg>.state_dict in loop.py:_payload :395, plus a C-stage row in LOOP_ORDER and _CALLS["C"];
  - a restore path: an ASSEMBLY_ORDER restore row BEFORE OPT.build if it owns parameters, as WORLD.load_into does (compose.py:2427-2436);
  - a geometry rule: EXACT or MAY_WIDEN fields in compose.py:_geometry_manifest (:3077-3181).
- ckpt/api.py:1037-1042 REFUSES a checkpoint that lacks a manifest field, so adding fields makes every existing text checkpoint non-resumable unless a rule for absent fields is ruled on.
- OPT.load_state refuses any param-group tensor-count change (opt/api.py:237-247). Only dim-0 widening is padded (Q-OPT-8).
- lm.vocab_slots is MAY_WIDEN with the rationale "a smaller checkpoint is a prefix" (compose.py:3097). Reserved codec ids must therefore sit at a fixed base that does not move when vocab_slots widens.

COUNTERS (DID IT FIRE)
- ABSENT means unreachable on this arm. PRESENT-AND-0 means armed and did not fire. Three-state Gates use spine/gate.py (Gate :27, three_state :80), and `reason` is required when unreachable.
- Counters must be seeded before the gate decides. world/api.py:600's `world.forecast.calls` is the model.
- A new package must expose counters(...) and be collected at an R row. The null or disabled arm must be a first-class configuration that returns inert answers (the WORLD D4 pattern, world/api.py:96-186), not None.
- Every param-owning object must expose parameters(). compose.py:_base_parameters walks an explicit list (:2854) and only WARNS when one is missing. WORLD ran with frozen random weights for this reason until World.parameters existed.

RNG
- Each drawing package needs a name in RNG_SUBSYSTEMS (compose.py:124). K8 refuses .get() and undeclared names, and A7 audits the accounting. Per-area children are derived, for example `data.synth.<label>` and `data.holdout.<key>`.
- Probes run under frozen_rng on their own stream (G7).

CONTRACT AND FROZEN SIGNATURES
- docs/04_CONTRACT.md §7 (:5341) is the normative list of 137 entry points. K1 compares it with src/<pkg>/api.py in BOTH directions, using ast.unparse of the argument list.
- A signature moves only by an owner ruling (a ### Q-<PKG>-n entry in §5) and an edit to §7 and the tree in the SAME commit. Every prose restatement of the count must move too, and K13 checks the numbers. Precedents: Q-LM-12 added LM.embed (122 -> 123); Q-FAB-13 added OPT.remap_rows; Q-OPT-4 removed a parameter; Q-CKPT-3 widened CKPT.save.
- Each entry point needs the docstring triple LEVERS READ / WIRES READ / DID IT FIRE, parsed by K4 and K5.
- Each entry point must be named by an ASSEMBLY_ORDER or LOOP_ORDER row, or listed in DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS with a reason naming EVERY required argument that has no producer (K6, K12).
- Every required argument must be produced by an EARLIER row's `produces` column, named in the row's note, or listed in ROW_ARGUMENTS_ELSEWHERE (K10). The column spells the consumer's name, and K11 refuses fabricated produces tokens.
- The root may read only declared Config names (K7).
- loop.py's _CALLS must agree per stage with LOOP_ORDER, or run() raises (loop.py:593-629).
- Other checks a new package trips: tests/test_contract K1-K16, test_ownership O1-O15 (O12/O13 citation checks resolve every `file.py::symbol` citation in prose), test_census N1-N8, test_assemble A1-A10 (the rendered docs are current), test_couplings, test_determinism and test_resume (bit-exact resume), and test_causality (the Q-FAB-7 no-peek rule applies to any media signature or sample: it must end before the window being predicted).

OWNER DECISIONS TO RESPECT
- WORLD stays enabled and must be part of multimodal training. WORLD_FEEDBACK ships False (world/levers.py:211-217; docs/04_CONTRACT.md:3554-3577), but the wiring must keep working.
- Codecs are learned from scratch, which means codec training is a new loss term and a new parameter group or tensor list inside OPT's accounting.
- Synthetic data first, with real data later into the same slots. The Stream/Areas record must be modality-generic now.
- Nothing may be removed or downgraded: bytes/token-based text behaviour must stay bit-identical at the default (media off). By the D4 pattern, "off" must mean the code path exists and is inert.

THROUGHPUT
- Measured on CPU in a scratch copy, 30 windows, 1 thread (ctx_probe.py):
  - GRU: ctx 128 -> 3.64 win/s (466 tok/s); ctx 512 -> 2.40 win/s (1226 tok/s).
  - Transformer: ctx 128 -> 2.97 win/s; ctx 512 -> 2.27 win/s.
- On CPU the per-window fixed cost dominates, so 4x tokens per window costs about 1.3-1.5x per window. That cost is the A-stage Python per window: SIG.encode on one sample, DOM.observe and TOK.on_window at loop.py:954-1023, plus the fabric. GPU behaviour is unmeasured here.

WHY (a) STRAINS THE TEXT PATH MORE
It reuses every existing surface (ids, the one softmax, next-token CE, MEM's next-token retrieval, DOM token priors, WORLD's obs_emb) at the cost of TOK/SIG/LM surgery and much longer sequences. Throughput is the stated constraint: a 1 s, 16 kHz clip at a 50 Hz, 4-codebook codec is 200 ids, over LM_CTX=128 today.

WHY (b) STRAINS WORLD AND THE LM INPUT CONTRACT
WORLD today is a per-position MLP into lat=32 with linear residual predictors and no history (world/api.py:234, :352-379). LM has no continuous input path. It keeps TOK and MEM text-only and matches the owner's "world model included" wish more literally.

A HYBRID IS THE LEAST INVASIVE
Discrete codec ids in the stream (for understanding and generation by the LM), with the codec's continuous pre-quantisation latents also fed to WORLD as a second obs source. WORLD's obs_emb hook already accepts any (B, L, width) tensor.

map.risks:
Ranked by how silently each one breaks.

1. bytes_per_token and the frozen signature width move under text when media shares the build corpus. MEASURED with bpt_probe.py in scratch, on the synthetic 4-area default:
   - text only: build bpt 1.502, SIG width 192.
   - text + a 256-symbol "codec" byte area: build bpt 1.366, width 174.
   - Text-only segmentation bpt was unchanged at 1.549 in both.

   So adding a media area to TOK's build input silently shrinks every TEXT window's routing signature by 9% for the whole run. The width is frozen once (compose.py:2803-2816), which also feeds data_plan's splice_window gate (data/api.py:1152) and RUN.bench bytes_per_window. Nothing reports it as a modality effect. Rule: bpt must be measured on text only.

2. Byte-level BPE eats codec streams. If codec ids are serialised as bytes:
   - _segment's greedy longest match (tok/api.py:1264-1304) assigns TEXT merge ids to codec byte runs that happen to match (for example the pair "th").
   - on_window/mint_burst (:1607, :1869) mint cross-code merges that compete with text for the soft cap and the 4096 ceiling.
   - DOM's retok decay and LM's new_row_init then treat them as text tokens.

   If codec ids are instead appended as ids outside id2bytes, every id2bytes[i] / bytes_per_id[i] read (Vocabulary.decode, blen, the mint pair concatenation) indexes past the table.

3. Dead-row masking kills codec rows. LM.decode masks `dead[int(live_vocab):] = True` with live_vocab = Vocabulary.size() (lm/api.py:816; _head at compose.py:3472-3490). Codec ids placed above BPE's live size get -inf at LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1. At =0 they sit in the text softmax denominator, and every text prediction pays for codec rows. CAP's vocab arm (at_cap compares len(id2bytes)) and TOK's ceiling would also count or mis-count reserved rows.

4. Geometry and resume.
   - New manifest fields make every existing checkpoint non-resumable: "A missing field is refused rather than skipped" (ckpt/api.py:1037-1042).
   - OPT refuses any tensor-count change (opt/api.py:237-247).
   - vocab_slots is MAY_WIDEN on a prefix argument (compose.py:3097), so a codec block anchored at the TOP of the table moves when vocab_slots widens.

   Goal B's natural experiment, resuming a text run and adding a modality as a new area, is blocked by three guards unless the owner rules on how they treat absent or new state.

5. Domain assignment by byte signature. SIG is a bag-of-units mean embedding (sig/api.py:171) with 64 dimensions trained contrastively. Proposal 01 predicts that modality becomes the dominant variance and the dimensions go to separating image or audio from text instead of kinds of text (docs/proposals/01_MODALITIES.md:57-76). This is unmeasured, and measuring it (M2) is proposal step 1.

   DOM thresholds (spawn 0.35, merge 0.28, radius quantiles) were tuned on byte windows. The _sample_window left-pad is byte 0 or token 0 (compose.py:3451-3458), and a pad of 0 is a real codec code. The Q-FAB-7 causality rule (the sample must end before the predicted window) applies to any media sample.

6. The per-source memory floor dilutes. The floor is src_share x capacity / live_sources (memory/api.py:829; DOM.manage's mem_floor_entries). Every media domain DOM spawns is a new source, so text domains' protected memory shrinks with no text-side change. FAB's breadth cap (FAB_DOM_FRAC=0.1 of live_domains, _breadth_ban fabric/api.py:1794) and DOM's cull budget move the same way.

7. Byte-offset coordinates. Segmentation.byte_pos is the stable coordinate for MEM positions (memory/api.py:1255: "MUST BE THE TRUE BYTE OFFSET"; fed at loop.py:2131), for the SIG cursor (compose.py:3367-3389), and for EVAL's held-out windows. Codec tokens have no bytes: a fake offset silently corrupts MEM's recall-span logic and SIG's cursor.

8. Metrics in bits per byte. CurveReading.per_domain_bpb, OPT's best_bpb, CKPT Retention.consider(curve_bpb) and DOM.note_competence (bits per window, loop.py:2264-2267) all assume one unit. A codec token carries very different information per id than a text token, so a mixed per-window loss makes DOM competence, FAB comp_ema culls and grow plateaus compare incomparable numbers. Proposal M3 is still open.

   Codec training adds its own loss to `total` (loop.py:1871). A bad weight there is the WORLD_W folding defect (world/api.py:381 docstring) in a new place.

9. WORLD is structurally weak for media. It is per-position and memoryless: an MLP to lat=32, linear residual predictors, horizon in "tokens" (world/levers.py:439), refused at horizon >= LM_CTX (world/api.py:1149).
   - Discrete: its horizon counts interleaved ids, so predicting t+1 across a text/codec boundary is a different task at every position.
   - Continuous: extra= enters AFTER the LM trunk (lm/api.py:666/708), so media cannot flow through the recurrence or attention.
   - WORLD_FEEDBACK=0 already measured within noise for text.
   - WORLD.manage (growth) is still deferred (compose.py DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS).

10. Throughput. LM_CTX=128 and pos_max = ctx are EXACT geometry. Audio at a 50 Hz x 4-codebook codec is 200 ids per second, and 64x64 video with 8x8 patches is 64 ids per frame. The GPU run already falls from about 38 to 2-3 windows/s late. The per-window A stage (one SIG.encode, DOM.observe and TOK.on_window per window, loop.py:954-1023) is a fixed Python cost; on CPU it dominated (ctx 128 -> 512 cost only about 1.35-1.5x per window). GPU is unmeasured. Longer windows also multiply MEM writes (one candidate per position) and the WORLD per-position MLP.

11. Synthetic data has no holdout. source=synthetic "holds nothing out" (data/api.py:455-457), so on a synthetic-first media phase the R matrix, retention and forgetting numbers (goal B) have nothing to measure against, and nothing refuses.

12. The optimizer can silently leave codecs untrained. compose.py:_base_parameters walks a fixed three-object list (:2854) and only warns on a missing parameters(). A learned-from-scratch codec that is not added there trains nothing, the same defect WORLD had until 2026-09-22 (world/api.py:141-175).

13. Contract drift. K1 fails in both directions. The §7 count (137) and its four prose restatements must move together. K10/K12 need every new argument produced or deferred with every missing producer named. loop._CALLS must match LOOP_ORDER per stage or run() raises. The docs/03 and docs/05 renders must be regenerated. The census needs an amendment row per new lever.

PROJECT CONTEXT USED (read-only):

=== A. EARLY-FUSION UNIFIED TOKEN MODELS (understand AND generate) ===

A1. Chameleon (Chameleon Team, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09818 [S]
- What they built: one transformer over text plus discrete image tokens. A 512x512 image becomes 1024 tokens from an 8192-entry codebook. Sizes 7B and 34B, 4.4T tokens, 4k context. They report beating Llama-2 on text-only tasks, and it generates images.
- The key finding for us: when all weights are shared, "each modality will try to compete with the other by increasing its norms slightly". Softmax is translation invariant, so logit norms drift, and training diverges late (after 20-30% of training). The 7B model without QK-Norm diverged after about 20% of an epoch.
- Fixes: QK-Norm, z-loss 1e-5, dropout 0.1 (7B), and Swin-style norm reordering (34B). Rising output norm of the last layer predicted a later divergence.
- Transfer: the image tokenizer was trained separately before the LM, so this is not end-to-end. The competition/norm-growth mechanism does not depend on scale and applies to our transformer arm.

A2. AnyGPT (Zhan, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12226 [S]; README https://github.com/OpenMOSS/AnyGPT [P]
- LLaMA-2 plus pretrained tokenizers: SpeechTokenizer for speech, SEED for images, Encodec-32k for music.
- Decoding goes through separate pretrained decoders (SoundStorm, an unCLIP SD-UNet, Encodec).
- No architecture change; new modalities enter only as data. Training uses 108k synthesized any-to-any dialogues.
- The README admits "generation may still be unstable".
- Transfer: shows that vocabulary extension alone gives any-to-any. But it rests entirely on pretrained codecs and a pretrained LLM, both of which the owner excludes.

A3. Unified-IO 2 (Lu, 2023/CVPR 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.17172 [S]
- The first autoregressive model that both understands and generates image, text, audio and action. It is an encoder-decoder, 1B/3B/7B, "trained from scratch".
- Data: 1B image-text pairs, 1T text tokens, 180M video clips. About 1T tokens over 1.5M steps at batch 512.
- Audio output: their own ViT-VQGAN on spectrograms, 256x128 becomes 512 tokens from an 8196-entry codebook.
- Image and audio history is compressed by a perceiver resampler to 32 and 16 tokens.
- Stabilizers: 2D RoPE, QK-norm, dynamic packing; objective is a multimodal mixture of denoisers.
- Caveat: image inputs go through a PRE-TRAINED ViT, so "from scratch" covers the transformer only.

A4. Emu3 (Wang, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18869 [S]; README https://github.com/baaivision/emu3 [P]
- A single transformer trained from scratch with next-token prediction only, over text, image and video.
- Vision tokenizer (MoVQGAN plus 3D-conv temporal residual layers): a 4x512x512 clip or one 512x512 image becomes 4096 tokens from a 32,768 codebook. That is 4x temporal and 8x8 spatial compression.
- Tokenizer loss: L2 + LPIPS + GAN + commitment. The tokenizer was trained before the LM on LAION-HR and InternVid.
- Loss balance: Emu3.5 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26583) [S] weights visual-token loss by 0.5 "to prevent visual tokens from overwhelming". I did not verify whether the original Emu3 does the same.

A5. VideoPoet (Kondratyuk, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14125 [S]
- A decoder LM over MAGVIT-v2 video/image tokens and SoundStream audio tokens.
- A 17-frame, 2.125 s, 128x128 clip at 8 fps becomes a (5,16,16) latent, i.e. 1280 tokens.
- Vocabulary layout: 256 special/task codes, then 262,144 visual codes (2^18), then 4,096 audio codes.
- Pretraining is a task mixture with prefix/output split and loss on the output only: text-to-video, image-to-video, future prediction, audio-to-video, and so on.
- A separate bidirectional windowed-attention module does super-resolution.
- The 8B size is (unverified).

A6. Gemini 1.0 (Gemini Team, 2023), https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/gemini/gemini_1_report.pdf [P]
- Quoted: "multimodal from the beginning and can natively output images using discrete image tokens".
- Visual encoding is "inspired by ... Flamingo, CoCa, PaLI".
- Video is "a sequence of frames in the large context window".
- Audio is ingested "at 16kHz from Universal Speech Model (USM) features".
- The report says joint training across text, image, audio and video gave state of the art in every domain, while "questions remain around finding the optimal dataset distribution".
- So Gemini is continuous-encoder input plus discrete-token image output, not all-discrete. USM is a pretrained encoder.

A7. SpeechGPT (Zhang, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11000 [S]
- HuBERT discrete units are added to an LLM vocabulary.
- Three stages: modality-adaptation pretraining, cross-modal instruction tuning, chain-of-modality tuning.
- The 1000 k-means units and LLaMA-13B base are (unverified).

A8. Scaling Laws for Native Multimodal Models (Shukor, 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07951 [S]
- 457 models trained from scratch. The most directly relevant paper for small from-scratch training.
- "Early-fusion exhibits stronger performance at lower parameter counts, is more efficient to train". Late fusion has no inherent advantage.
- MoE lets the model "learn modality-specific weights, significantly enhancing performance". Experts specialize by modality mostly in the early and last layers.
- Learned (modality-agnostic) routing beat hard modality-aware routing on image-caption and interleaved data.

A9. Scaling Laws for Generative Mixed-Modal LMs (Aghajanyan, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.03728 [S]
- 250+ runs from 8M to 30B parameters, 7 modalities, 5-100B tokens.
- Adds a synergy/competition term to unimodal scaling laws.
- Observed "emergent coordinate-ascent style training that naturally alternates between modalities" and a link between modality competition and training instability.
- A 30B speech-text model beat the unimodal models. The claim that competition dominates at small scale and synergy appears with size is (unverified) in detail.

A10. 4M (Mizrahi, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.06647 [S]
- An any-to-any encoder-decoder trained with masked modeling over discrete tokens from per-modality tokenizers.
- Shows the "one tokenizer per modality, one shared trunk" pattern works at B/L sizes.

=== B. LATE FUSION / ADAPTERS (understanding only) ===

B1. Flamingo (Alayrac, 2022), https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/DeepMind.com/Blog/tackling-multiple-tasks-with-a-single-visual-language-model/flamingo.pdf [P]
- Design: a frozen Chinchilla LM (70B, so 80B total) plus a frozen vision encoder. A Perceiver Resampler maps frames sampled at 1 FPS to a few visual tokens. New GATED XATTN-DENSE layers are inserted between frozen LM layers with `y = y + tanh(alpha)*xattn(y,x)`, alpha initialized at 0.
- Output is text only. The model is "a visually-conditioned autoregressive text generation model", so it cannot generate images, audio or video.
- Measured ablations:
  - Removing the zero-init tanh gate costs 4.4% overall and causes "training instabilities, with high peaks randomly observed in the losses".
  - Training the LM from scratch: -10.2%. Training the vision encoder from scratch: -11.8%.
  - Unfreezing from pretrained weights: -3.9% (vision encoder) and -5.5% (LM). The authors call this catastrophic forgetting.
  - Co-training on MassiveText (weight 1.0, LM learning rate x0.1), i.e. replaying the LM's own pretraining data, was still worse than freezing: "the strategy of freezing the language model to avoid catastrophic forgetting is strong".

B2. LLaVA (Liu, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08485 [S]
- A pretrained CLIP ViT-L/14 is joined to Vicuna by a trainable projection.
- Stage 1 trains only the projection on 595K CC3M pairs. Stage 2 fine-tunes projection plus LLM on 158K instructions.
- Understanding only; output is text.

B3. Why these do not give generation. Output is only the LM's text head. Generation needs an output vocabulary or head in the target modality plus a decoder, which is what A1-A6 and C add.
- Janus (Wu, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13848 [S]: using one visual encoder for both directions compromises understanding, because understanding wants semantic features and generation wants detail. Janus splits the paths: SigLIP-style features in, VQ tokens out, one shared transformer.

=== C. CONTINUOUS-TOKEN GENERATION ===

C1. Transfusion (Zhou, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11039 [S]
- One transformer: next-token loss on text plus a diffusion loss on continuous image patches (VAE latents). Loss is L_LM + lambda*L_diff with lambda=5.
- Attention is causal for text and bidirectional within an image. Bidirectional helps: FID 61.3 to 20.3 with linear patch encoders.
- A U-Net patch encoder/decoder beats a linear one, and allows larger patches (1024 down to 16 patches per image).
- Trained from scratch up to 7B and 2T tokens.
- Against Chameleon: better text-to-image at less than 1/3 of the compute, and text perplexity parity at 50-60% fewer FLOPs.

C2. MAR / Diffusion Loss (Li, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11838 [S]
- A small denoising MLP models the per-token distribution of continuous tokens, so no vector quantization is needed.
- The masked-autoregressive variant predicts many tokens at once. FID 1.55 on ImageNet 256.
- The MLP head is small, so it fits a small model.

C3. GIVT (Tschannen, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.02116 [S]
- Linear input projection plus a Gaussian-mixture output head over beta-VAE latents.
- Beats VQ-GAN/MaskGIT. The simplest continuous head.

C4. Fluid (Fan, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13863 [S]
- All four variants scale in validation loss, but evaluation metrics diverge.
- Continuous tokens give "significantly better visual quality" than discrete. Random order beats raster order on GenEval.

C5. Show-o (Xie, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12528 [S]
- Autoregressive text plus discrete masked diffusion for image tokens, in one transformer.

C6. Diffusion Forcing (Chen, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01392 [S]
- Each token gets an independent noise level, and a causal model is trained to denoise.
- Rolls continuous video out past the training horizon where baselines diverge. Proposed as a world-model backbone.

=== D. TOKENIZERS, SEQUENCE LENGTH, INTERLEAVING ===

D1. FSQ (Mentzer, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15505 [S]
- Replaces VQ with a few dimensions (<10), each rounded to a fixed small set of values.
- "Does not suffer from codebook collapse and does not need ... commitment losses, codebook reseeding, code splitting, entropy penalties". Cost versus VQ is about 0.5-3%.
- The most robust option for training a codec from scratch.

D2. MAGVIT-v2 (Yu, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05737 [S]
- Lookup-free quantization gives a very large vocabulary (2^18 in VideoPoet). A causal 3D CNN handles image and video jointly.
- The paper's thesis: "tokenizer is key".

D3. SoundStream (Zeghidour, 2021), https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.03312 [S]
- Conv encoder/decoder plus residual VQ, trained end to end with adversarial and reconstruction losses.
- Quantizer dropout lets one model serve 3-18 kbps.

D4. AudioLM (Borsos, 2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03143 [S]
- Semantic tokens (w2v-BERT) for long-range structure, then coarse, then fine acoustic tokens (SoundStream RVQ).

D5. MusicGen (Copet, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05284 [S]
- EnCodec with 4 codebooks of 2048.
- The "delay" interleaving pattern cuts autoregressive steps 4x versus flattening at similar quality.

D6. Moshi (Défossez, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00037 [S]; README https://github.com/kyutai-labs/moshi [P]
- Mimi codec: 24 kHz audio to 12.5 Hz frames, 1.1 kbps. The first codebook is distilled toward WavLM semantics.
- A small Depth Transformer models the codebooks within one time step; a 7B Temporal Transformer models time. So sequence length is set by frame rate, not frame rate times codebooks.
- "Inner monologue": text tokens aligned to its own speech "greatly improves the quality". User and model audio are parallel streams.

D7. WavTokenizer (Ji, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.16532 [S]
- A single quantizer at 40 or 75 tokens/s for 24 kHz audio, against DAC's 9 quantizers at 900 tokens/s.

D8. Spirit LM (Nguyen, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05755 [S]
- Interleaves speech and text at the word level: modality switches at random word boundaries in aligned data, and speech units are deduplicated.
- Gives few-shot cross-modal ASR/TTS.

D9. LWM (Liu, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08268 [S]
- Video plus language up to 1M tokens. Context grows progressively from 4K to 1M.
- Uses masked sequence packing and "loss weighting to balance language and vision".

D10. Genie (Bruce, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15391 [S]
- A world model: an ST-transformer VQ video tokenizer, a latent-action model and an autoregressive dynamics model, all trained unsupervised on video, 11B.

D11. V-JEPA (Bardes, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08471 [S]
- Predicts masked video regions in latent space with no decoder and no pixel loss. Understanding only, which is the same class as our current WORLD objective.

|---|---|---|
| Chameleon | one 512^2 image | 1024 |
| Emu3 | 4 frames at 512^2 | 4096 |
| VideoPoet | 2.1 s video at 128^2 | 1280 |
| Moshi / Mimi | audio | 12.5 frames/s, codebooks absorbed by the depth transformer |
| WavTokenizer | audio | 40-75 tokens/s |
| DAC | audio | 900 tokens/s |
| Unified-IO 2 | image / audio history | resampled to 32 / 16 |

Against LM_CTX=128, a naive multi-codebook codec leaves under 0.2 s of audio per window. A 12.5-50 Hz single-codebook (or depth-factored) codec gives 2.5-10 s.

=== E. MODALITY-SPECIFIC LOSSES AND BALANCING ===

E1. Weights seen in the papers:
- Transfusion: lambda=5 on the diffusion loss.
- Emu3.5: 0.5 on vision tokens.
- LWM: explicit language/vision loss weighting.
- VideoPoet: loss only on the output segment.

E2. DeepSeek-VL (Lu, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05525 [S]
- About 70% multimodal / 30% text-only during joint pretraining to keep language ability. Also "modality warm-up" (multimodal share ramps up linearly) and modality-pure batches.

E3. Gradient-Blending (Wang, 2020), https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.12681 [S]
- A multimodal network is often beaten by its best unimodal part, because modalities overfit and generalize at different rates. They blend using an overfitting-to-generalization ratio.

E4. OGM-GE (Peng, 2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15332 [S]
- A dominant modality leaves the others under-optimized. Fix: modulate each modality's gradient by the gap in its contribution, and add Gaussian noise.
- E3 and E4 are discriminative settings, but the mechanism is the same competition as A1 and A9.

E5. Chameleon (A1): competition shows up as norm growth, and output norm is a leading indicator of divergence.

=== F. CONTINUAL / SEQUENTIAL LEARNING ACROSS MODALITIES ===

F1. Parameter isolation beats replay for protecting an existing skill:
- Flamingo (B1): freezing beats MassiveText co-training.
- LMFusion (Shi, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15188 [S]: Llama-3 text modules frozen, plus parallel image-only QKV/FFN/norm modules with shared attention. It "maintain[s] Llama-3's language capabilities". Against from-scratch training it gives +20% image understanding and +3.6% generation at 50% of the FLOPs.

F2. Modality-specific parameters with shared attention:
- BEiT-3 (Wang, 2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10442 [S]: Multiway transformer, 1.9B = 692M vision FFN experts + 692M language FFN experts + 52M VL experts + 317M shared attention.
- VLMo (Bao, 2021), https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.02358 [S]: MoME, trained stagewise (image-only, then text-only, then joint). That the attention was frozen during the text stage is (unverified).
- Mixture-of-Transformers (Liang, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04996 [S]: all non-embedding parameters untied per modality, global attention. Matches dense Chameleon-7B at 55.8% of FLOPs, and matches speech at 37.2%. In the Transfusion setting, 760M MoT beats 1.4B dense on image metrics.
- MoMa (Lin, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.21770 [S]: 4 text + 4 image expert groups with learned routing inside each group. 3.7x overall FLOPs saving (2.6x text, 5.2x image) at 1T tokens and 1.4B, against 3x for 8 mixed experts.
- Conflict with A8, which found learned routing beats hard modality routing. Hard modality groups plus learned routing inside each group (MoMa) is the combination that won in the source that tested both.

F3. MoE-LLaVA (Lin, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.15947 [S]
- Stage III copies the trained FFN into every expert ("upcycling") and trains only the MoE layers and routers.
- 2.2B active parameters, comparable to InternVL-Chat-19B, best on POPE hallucination.

F4. LIMoE (Mustafa, 2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.02770 [S]
- Modality-specific experts emerge on their own in a shared MoE, but only with local/global entropy regularizers for stability and balance.
- Result: 78.6% ImageNet zero-shot against CLIP's 76.2%.

F5. Forgetting when a modality or task is added to an MLLM:
- EMT (Zhai, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10313 [S]: early fine-tuning helps other datasets, but "excessive fine-tuning" causes forgetting and hallucination even with a frozen encoder.
- Wings (Zhang, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03496 [S]: text-only forgetting follows an attention shift from pre-image to post-image text. Parallel low-rank "learners" with a router fix it.
- CoIN (Chen, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08350 [S]: forgetting is mostly lost instruction alignment, not lost knowledge. MoELoRA helps.

F6. Modality-incremental methods:
- PathWeave (Yu, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20178 [S]: adds image, video, audio, depth and point cloud one at a time using adapter-in-adapter plus MoE gating, training 98.73% fewer parameters.
- MERA (Zhang, 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07663 [S]: modality-incremental learning suffers forgetting AND misalignment between shared and modality-specific parts. Merge-then-realign keeps 99.84% backward relative gain over 4 added modalities.
- MICL (Pian, 2024/TMLR 2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.13050 [S]: modality shift and task-type shift each cause forgetting. Fix: pseudo-targets plus instruction-conditioned distillation.

F7. Expert expansion and routing in continual learning:
- Lifelong-MoE (Chen, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.12281 [S]: add experts per new distribution, freeze old experts and gates, KL regularization on outputs.
- MoE-Adapters (Yu, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11549 [S]: a distribution discriminator sends out-of-distribution inputs to the original model.
- Theory on MoE in CL (Li, 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16437 [S]: experts specialize per task, but the gate must STOP updating after enough rounds to converge. More experts need more rounds.

F8. Replay:
- Ibrahim (2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08763 [S]: learning-rate re-warm, re-decay and replay match full retraining at 405M, including English to German. The exact replay fractions are (unverified).
- TiC-CLIP (Garg, 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16226 [S]: warm start plus replay costs 2.5x less compute than retraining.
- Deep Generative Replay (Shin, 2017), https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08690 [S]: a generator replays old tasks.

F9. Gap: I found no paper that adds audio or video, one after another, to a small model trained entirely from scratch, generating in every modality, with learned codecs. Every continual-modality result above sits on a pretrained LLM and usually pretrained encoders.

=== G. WHAT TRANSFERS TO THIS PROJECT (small GRU/transformer, width 128, from scratch, synthetic first) ===

G1. Scale gap. The evidence runs from 8M (Aghajanyan) through 0.16B-7B (Transfusion, Shukor) to 80B (Flamingo), on 1e10-1e12 tokens. Absolute numbers will not carry over. What carries over is structure: modality-specific parameters, zero-init gates, QK-norm/z-loss, collapse-free quantizers, depth-factored codebooks, per-modality loss normalization, freezing or isolation for protection, and replay.

G2. The fabric already is the right shape. A8, F2 and F4 all say a routed expert population should specialize by modality, and that doing so saves FLOPs (MoT 55.8%, MoMa 3.7x). This supports Proposal 02: modality at the top level, learned routing inside it.
- LIMoE (F4) needed entropy regularizers to prevent collapse. FAB_BALANCE, FAB_DOM_FRAC and FAB_EC_W are this project's equivalents.
- F7's theory says to freeze gates once specialized. That bears on how the fabric keeps routing stable for old modalities while it grows.

G3. The zero-init gate pattern from Flamingo is the pattern this tree already uses for world_proj (Q-WORLD-10). Flamingo measured it: 4.4% and stability. It is the evidence-backed way to attach any new modality pathway to the LM.

G4. Understanding versus generation conflict (Janus) is real at scale. For a width-128 model it is untested, so it is a measurement to make, not a default.

G5. Continuous heads beat discrete on quality per FLOP (Transfusion, Fluid). But discrete tokens:
- give an exact likelihood, so bits/byte-style metrics survive (M3);
- reuse TOK, LM_VOCAB_SLOTS, the memory store's token codes and DOM token histograms;
- are what every from-scratch any-to-any system here (Unified-IO 2, Emu3, Chameleon) used.

G6. Every surveyed system trained its tokenizer FIRST and froze it. For a system that must keep learning, a codec that keeps learning shifts what each token means under the LM. I found no source addressing that. It is the same problem the tree already solves for TOK re-segmentation (anchor/new_row_init) and MEM_REKEY_EVERY.

G7. Throughput. Sequence length is the dominant cost (the 20k-window GPU run already slows from 38 to 2-3 windows/s). The literature's answers are:
- aggressive temporal compression (Emu3 4x, Mimi 12.5 Hz);
- depth-factored codebooks (Moshi) or the delay pattern (MusicGen, 4x fewer steps);
- resampler compression of context history (Unified-IO 2: 32/16 tokens);
- modality-sparse compute (MoT/MoMa).
lit.recommendations:
These are ranked. Each is phrased as an A/B arm or a measurement, because performance decides. Nothing below removes an existing function.

R1. Architecture: early fusion into ONE sequence, with modality-partitioned sparsity in the fabric.
- Build it MoMa-style: hard modality groups of experts, learned routing inside each group, shared attention/GRU trunk.
- MoT-style untying of norms and projections per modality is the next arm.
- Evidence: Shukor 2025 (early fusion wins at low parameter counts; MoE modality specialization helps); MoMa 3.7x; MoT 55.8%/37.2% FLOPs; BEiT-3/VLMo.
- In this tree:
  - modality becomes the top level of routing (Proposal 02);
  - each modality gets its own fabric group, so the breadth cap and growth/cull act inside it;
  - MEM_OWNERS partitions become per-modality owner blocks;
  - adding a modality counts as adding an area/domain for the goal-B benchmark (answers M10: yes).
- Settle the MoMa-versus-Shukor routing conflict with one measurement: hard groups against learned routing, at the tree's scale.

R2. Protection when a modality is added: isolation first, replay second, both as arms.
- Default arm (LMFusion/Flamingo pattern): freeze or learning-rate-shield the text experts and text rows while a new modality's experts and rows train. The new pathway attaches through ZERO-INIT tanh gates, the same pattern as world_proj.
- Initialize new modality experts by copying trained text experts (MoE-LLaVA upcycling), which is the analogue of LM_NEW_ROW_INIT='mean'.
- Second arm: replay of old-modality windows from the memory store, or generative self-replay (Shin 2017). The model generates every modality, so it can replay its own old outputs.
- Third arm: learning-rate re-warm on the modality boundary (Ibrahim 2024). OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM already exists for this.
- Measure every arm on the R matrix: held-out bits per token of each old modality before and after each addition. Flamingo's result (freezing beats replay at weight 1.0) is the prior to beat.

R3. Codecs learned from scratch: FSQ quantizers, a single codebook or depth-factored codebooks, strong temporal compression.
- Audio: 1-D conv encoder/decoder with FSQ at about 25-50 frames/s.
  - One codebook: WavTokenizer shows a single quantizer suffices.
  - Several codebooks: model them with a small depth head per time step (Moshi) or the delay pattern (MusicGen), so the LM sequence grows with frame rate only.
- Video: 3D-conv (MAGVIT-v2/Emu3 style) encoder with 4x temporal and 8x8 spatial compression, FSQ codes. For synthetic 32x32 or 64x64 frames that is 16-64 tokens per 4 frames.
- Loss: L2 plus a perceptual/spectral term. Leave GAN terms as a later arm.
- Why FSQ: it removes codebook collapse and its fixes (commitment, reseeding), which is the main failure risk for a small from-scratch codec.
- Train the codec in its own phase and freeze it (every surveyed system did). A later arm: codec updates with a re-tokenization handover modelled on the TOK/anchor mechanism and MEM rekey.
- Package placement: codecs live in their own packages (AUD, VID) with their own levers (M4). Their token-rate numbers are MEASURED quantities, i.e. a derive conversion, not a wire.

R4. Discrete tokens first, a continuous head as a planned arm.
- Discrete FSQ codes enter separate vocabulary ranges. This keeps exact likelihood for M3 (bits per token of each modality's codes, plus codec reconstruction error reported separately) and reuses TOK, vocab_slots, the memory store and DOM histograms.
- Then add a MAR/GIVT-style small continuous head (MLP diffusion or Gaussian-mixture over codec latents) as an arm judged on generation quality per FLOP. Transfusion and Fluid say it should win; at width 128 that is unmeasured.

R5. Loss balancing as per-modality levers owned by each modality package.
- Normalize each modality's loss per token of that modality.
- Start with the published weights as prior values: vision/video token weight 0.5 (Emu3.5), text-only share of at least 30% (DeepSeek-VL), and a linear modality warm-up.
- Add a did-it-fire instrument for modality competition: per-modality output-norm and logit-norm growth. Chameleon found norm growth predicts divergence 20-30% into training.
- For the transformer arm, add QK-norm and z-loss (1e-5). Flag OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 as a risk for multimodal runs (Chameleon, Unified-IO 2, Aghajanyan all tie modality competition to instability).

R6. Synthetic-first data built so that understanding AND generation can be scored exactly.
- Generators with known parameters:
  - video: moving sprites or bouncing shapes with known positions, velocities, colours;
  - audio: tone, chirp and note sequences from Markov processes, extending DATA_N_PROCESSES;
  - text captions: derived from the same parameters.
- Train with VideoPoet-style task prefixes (caption to video, video to caption, audio to caption, future prediction), loss on the output segment.
- Scoring: understanding by caption accuracy against the true parameters; generation by running a parameter-recovery probe on the generated clip. That gives an exact generation metric that bits/byte cannot.
- Add Spirit-LM word-level interleaving for audio and text, and Moshi's "inner monologue" (text aligned to generated audio) as an arm.

R7. WORLD in multimodal training.
- Its present objective (latent t+1 with VICReg) is JEPA-like, an understanding objective (V-JEPA).
- Make WORLD predict codec latents of the next video/audio chunk. Generation then comes from the frozen codec decoder, as in Genie (tokenizer, then dynamics).
- Keep WORLD_FEEDBACK False by default with the zero-born projection. Re-test feedback on video, where forecasting has more to offer than on text.
- A Diffusion-Forcing head (per-token noise levels) is the later arm for long rollouts.

R8. Throughput budget before building.
- Fix a tokens-per-second budget per modality so that LM_CTX=128 covers at least a few seconds of audio or a few frames of video.
- Compress history with a resampler (Unified-IO 2: 32/16 tokens) rather than lengthening windows.
- Treat modality-sparse compute (R1) as a throughput measure, not only a quality one.
- Decide M1 (one Windows clock or one per modality) before writing the codecs, as the proposal already says.

R9. Build order, consistent with Proposal 01:
1. Text sampler.
2. The M2 signature measurement on text plus codec tokens. The literature predicts the leading signature dimensions will separate modality (LIMoE and Shukor both find modality specialization emerging), which supports the hierarchy.
3. Audio codec (FSQ), then audio understand plus generate with isolation plus zero-init gates, then the R matrix.
4. Video codec, then video, with WORLD attached.
5. The continuous-head and codec-drift arms.

Q1. Primary texts. Most claims are [S] (search excerpts of the paper's own page), because the proxy blocks arxiv, openreview, huggingface and CVF. Only Gemini 1.0 and Flamingo were read in full. Before any number here becomes a default, someone should read these in full: Transfusion (lambda, attention ablations), MoMa (group routing details, plus how mixture-of-depths interacts with it), Shukor 2025 (the learned-versus-modality-aware routing result, which conflicts with MoMa), Aghajanyan (which modality pairs compete at small scale), and Emu3 (whether it used a vision loss weight).

Q2. Codec drift under continual learning. No source found. Is a codec that keeps learning compatible with an LM whose token meanings must stay stable? Options: freeze after a codec phase; a versioned codec with a TOK-style re-tokenization handover; EMA codec weights. This is a novel design question for goal B.

Q3. Hard modality groups (MoMa) or learned routing (Shukor), at width 128 with 2048 fabric experts? And must the gate stop updating for old modalities (Li 2024 theory), which interacts with fabric growth and cull?

Q4. Does the understanding/generation conflict (Janus) appear at this scale? It decides whether each modality needs two input paths (a semantic encoder in, codec tokens out) or one.

Q5. Discrete FSQ codes against a continuous diffusion/GMM head on synthetic data at small scale. Transfusion and Fluid favour continuous at 0.1B+. Nothing was measured at width 128. And what replaces bits/byte for the continuous arm, given diffusion gives only a bound?

Q6. Is freezing text experts (Flamingo, LMFusion) compatible with the owner's rule "never downgrade functionality"? Freezing stops text improving while the new modality trains. A learning-rate-shielded or replay arm may be required, and Flamingo measured freezing as better than replay at weight 1.0.

Q7. Clock kinds (M1). With 25-50 Hz audio and 4x-compressed video, what does one Window mean per modality, and which cadence levers (DOM_MANAGE_EVERY, FAB_COOLDOWN, MEM_REKEY_EVERY) need a named conversion in spine.derive?

Q8. Does multimodal training make the WORLD forecast worth feeding back? The within-noise text result (Q-WORLD-10) may not hold for video/audio, where next-chunk prediction carries more structure. This needs its own GPU experiment.

Q9. Is the 64-d byte signature (SIG_SPACE='bytes') meaningful over codec tokens, or does each modality need its own signature space (M2)? That measurement is the cheapest one here and should come first.

=== 1. MY MEASUREMENT: tiny from-scratch audio codec on procedural audio, CPU ===
Files, all in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/mm/research-codecs/:
- codec.py: generator, models, quantisers and metrics.
- codec_r3.py … codec_r6.py: exact per-round copies.
- results.tsv: every run in one table.
- r*_*.json and r*_*.log: per-run results and logs.

Setup:
- Data: 8 kHz procedural audio clips. Each clip mixes 1-2 events drawn from pure tones (80-2560 Hz), linear or exponential chirps, harmonic complexes, formant-vowel "syllables" with noise-burst consonants, and 8-note-scale melodies, with envelopes and optional noise.
- Training: fresh 0.5 s crops every step, batch 8.
- Held-out set: 16 clips of 2 s from a fixed seed.
- Model: SEANet-style 1-D conv encoder and decoder (C=16, ELU), about 0.65M parameters, stride 160 (50 Hz) or 320 (25 Hz).
- Loss: multi-scale log-mel + multi-scale STFT + waveform L1. No GAN.
- Optimiser: AdamW at 1e-3 with warmup, 1 CPU thread, 8 minutes per run, about 2,000-2,300 steps (about 8,000-9,000 s of audio seen).
- Reconstruction metric: DAC-style multi-scale log10-mel L1 ("mel", lower is better). Reference points:
  - silence: 1.83
  - 8-bit µ-law at 64 kbps: 0.50 (SNR 37.9 dB)
  - a decoder that ignores its codes and outputs the average spectrum (the collapsed runs below): about 1.12-1.19

Headline numbers (8 kHz, 8 minutes CPU):

| Run | Tokens/s | Nominal bit/s | Entropy bit/s | Codes used | Perplexity | mel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) FSQ 8,5,5,5 (1000 codes) + my entropy bonus, 50 Hz (r6_fsq50_ent) | 50 | 498 | 400 | 462/1000 | 254 | 0.678 |
| (b) Same, 25 Hz (r6_fsq25_ent) | 25 | 249 | 189 | 299/1000 | 188 | 0.746 |
| (c) Plain FSQ, 50 Hz (r5_fsq50; older-architecture r2_fsq) | 50 | 498 | – | 327 (r2: 217) | 114 (r2: 61) | 0.749 (r2: 0.666) |
| (d) Plain FSQ, 25 Hz (r5_fsq25) | 25 | 249 | – | 1 (collapsed) | – | 1.116 (= "ignore the codes") |
| (e) RVQ 4×256, 50 Hz (r2_rvq) | 200 flattened | 1600 | 1314 | 59-86% per level | – | 0.686 |
| (f) RVQ 4×256, 25 Hz (r6_rvq25) | 100 | 800 | – | 2-3 per level (collapsed) | – | 1.117 |
| (g) Continuous, no quantiser (r2_none) | – | – | – | – | – | 0.669 |

Notes on the table:
- (a) closes about 87% of the gap between silence and 8-bit µ-law on this metric. It is statistically at the continuous ceiling of the same architecture (g).
- (e) Adding RVQ levels 2-4 did not improve reconstruction: mel 0.696 / 0.702 / 0.692 / 0.686 for 1-4 levels, because the decoder was the bottleneck.
- (f) My dead-code threshold is set very leniently, so treat (f) as a weak RVQ baseline.

Phase is not learned at this scale:
- Every compressed run has SNR of about 0 dB and SI-SNR of about -45 dB. The codec reproduces the spectral envelope but not the waveform phase in about 2k steps.
- Sanity check (r5_sanity_s20): at almost no compression (stride 20, continuous 400 Hz latent), the same pipeline reaches SNR 8.8 dB and SI-SNR 4.9 dB in 4 minutes. So the code is fine. Waveform or phase fidelity at 25-50 Hz simply needs far more steps and/or adversarial losses, as every published codec uses.

STFT-domain (iSTFT-head, Vocos-style) variant, 6.4M params (r3, r4):
- Best continuous result: mel 0.558.
- Its FSQ collapsed to 1-3 codes even with GroupNorm before the projection.
- A phase-aware complex-STFT loss made it worse (it pulls the output toward zero).

Encode + decode speed of the 0.65M model: about 0.02-0.027 real-time factor on 1 CPU thread (about 40-50× faster than real time).

Main empirical lesson: from-scratch discrete bottlenecks collapse ("decoder learns to ignore the codes") at low frame rates under short budgets. FSQ is NOT immune: 3 of 5 plain-FSQ runs collapsed. A cheap per-dimension marginal-entropy bonus (LFQ/BSQ-style, soft assignment of each FSQ scalar to its grid, maximise the batch-average entropy; about 20 lines in FSQ.forward in codec.py) fixed collapse in both runs I tried (25 Hz: 1 → 299 codes; 50 Hz: 327 → 462) and improved reconstruction.

What this means for the LM:
- LM_CTX is 128 tokens per window.
- At 50 tokens/s, one window is 2.56 s of audio. At 25 tokens/s it is 5.1 s.
- RVQ 4×256 flattened (200 tokens/s) gives only 0.64 s per window.

=== 2. AUDIO CODECS (published) ===

SoundStream (Zeghidour, 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.03312) [S]:
- 24 kHz audio to 75 Hz embeddings.
- RVQ with up to 80 layers in experiments, 3-18 kbps.
- Quantizer dropout lets one model serve 3-18 kbps with negligible loss compared with fixed-rate models.
- AudioLM (Borsos, 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03143) [S] used SoundStream at stride 480 (50 Hz), 12 × 1024 RVQ = 6 kbps = 600 tokens/s. Its semantic tokens (w2v-BERT) run at 25 Hz with vocabulary 512.

EnCodec (Défossez, 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13438):
- [C] github.com/facebookresearch/encodec model.py and seanet.py: ratios [8,5,4,2] give hop 320, i.e. 75 Hz at 24 kHz. Bandwidths 1.5/3/6/12/24 kbps. n_q = 24000 // (75 × 10) = 32 codebooks of 1024 bins. So 150-2400 tokens/s.
- [C] core_vq.py: EMA codebook with decay 0.99, optional k-means init, dead-code expiry below an EMA count of 2, replaced with batch samples.
- [S] Training: 8 A100s, 300 epochs × 2000 updates, batch 64 × 1 s, Adam at 3e-4. That is about 600k updates, or about 10.7k hours of audio seen.

DAC, improved RVQGAN (Kumar, 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.06546):
- [C] conf/final/44khz.yml: rates [2,4,8,8] (hop 512, 86 Hz), 9 codebooks × 1024, codebook_dim 8, quantizer_dropout 0.5. That is 8 kbps, about 775 tokens/s.
- [C] conf/final/16khz.yml: rates [2,4,5,8] (50 Hz), 12 × 1024.
- [C] Training: 400k iterations, batch 72 × 0.38 s (about 3,000 hours seen), AdamW at 1e-4 with betas (0.8, 0.99), mel-loss weight 15.
- [C] quantize.py: factorised 8-d lookup plus L2-normalised codes, both credited to ViT-VQGAN.
- [S] These fixes improve codebook usage and therefore bitrate efficiency.

SpeechTokenizer (Zhang, 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.16692) [C]/[S]:
- 16 kHz, 50 Hz, 8 RVQ levels × 1024.
- RVQ-1 is distilled from HuBERT. This needs a pretrained teacher, so it violates the from-scratch rule.

Mimi / Moshi (Défossez, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00037):
- [C] moshi/models/loaders.py: 24 kHz, SEANet ratios [8,6,5,4] (hop 960, 25 Hz) then downsampled to FRAME_RATE 12.5. 32 codebooks of 2048 bins trained; Moshi uses 8.
- [S] 8 × 2048 at 12.5 Hz = 1.1 kbps = 100 tokens/s. One semantic VQ is distilled from WavLM (again a pretrained teacher).
- [S] Training: 4M steps, batch 128 × 12 s windows.
- [S] Applying quantisation only 50% of the time "significantly improves VisQOL". Adversarial-only training (no reconstruction loss) gave MUSHRA 81.0.

WavTokenizer (Ji, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.16532):
- [C] configs/…frame40…yaml: 24 kHz, hop 600 (40 Hz), a single codebook of 4096, k-means init with 200 iterations.
- [S] 40 or 75 tokens/s. Growing the codebook from 1024 to 4096 gained 0.55 UTMOS. The decoder attention block is critical. 3 s training context beats 1 s. UTMOS 4.05 at 0.9 kbps (75 tokens/s).

MusicGen (Copet, 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05284) [S]:
- EnCodec at 32 kHz, 4 × 2048 at 50 Hz.
- A delay pattern predicts all codebooks in parallel, so only 50 autoregressive steps per second of audio.

Low-rate FSQ speech codec (Parker, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19842) [S]: a large transformer with an FSQ bottleneck reaches state-of-the-art speech quality at 400 or 700 bps.

Vocos (Siuzdak, 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00814) [S]: an iSTFT head, about an order of magnitude faster than time-domain vocoders.

HILCodec (Ahn, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04752) [S]: a lightweight, low-MAC streaming codec (320-sample chunks).

=== 3. QUANTISERS AND COLLAPSE ===

VQ-VAE (van den Oord, 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00937) [S]: the original nearest-neighbour codebook with a straight-through estimator.

Standard fixes for codebook collapse:
- EMA updates, k-means init and dead-code restart. [C] EnCodec.
- Factorised low-dimensional plus L2-normalised codes: ViT-VQGAN (Yu, 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.04627) [S], adopted by DAC [C].
- The rotation trick (Fifty, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06424) [S]: improves reconstruction, codebook use and quantisation error across 11 VQ-VAE setups.
- SimVQ (Zhu, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.02038) [S]: a linear reparameterisation of the codebook gives near-full use even at 262k+ entries.

FSQ (Mentzer, 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15505) [C] README: needs no codebook, commitment loss, reseeding or entropy penalty, and "does not suffer from codebook collapse".
- iFSQ (Lin, 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17124) [S] disagrees: vanilla FSQ's tanh causes "activation collapse". They replace it with 2σ(1.6x)-1 and find about 4 bits per dimension optimal.
- My runs side with iFSQ. Plain FSQ collapsed in 3 of 5 runs, and the entropy bonus fixed it.

LFQ, MAGVIT-v2 (Yu, 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05737) [S]:
- Zero-dimensional codes, vocabulary 2^18.
- Needs an entropy loss (weight 0.1, 2000 annealing steps).
- BSQ (Zhao, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07548) [S] factorises that entropy term to O(L). My FSQ bonus is the same idea.

Cosmos uses FSQ with levels (8,8,8,5,5,5) = 64k codes [S]. The tokens are 1..64K and C=6 FSQ dimensions [C].

=== 4. VIDEO AND IMAGE TOKENIZERS ===

VQGAN (Esser, 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.09841) [S]: f=16 with 1024 or 16384 codes, and f=8 with 8192.

Chameleon (Chameleon team, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09818) [S]:
- 512² images become 1024 tokens from 8192 codes, inside a 65,536-token shared vocabulary.
- Divergence was traced to softmax when training on modalities of very different entropy.

VideoGPT (Yan, 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.10157) [C] README: 3-D conv VQ-VAE with defaults downsample 4×4×4, n_codes 2048, 2 GPUs × batch 16.

MAGVIT (Yu, 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.05199) [S]: 16 frames at 128² become 4×16×16 = 1024 tokens (4× temporal, 8× spatial), 1024 codes.

MAGVIT-v2 [S]:
- 17 frames at 128² become 5×16×16 tokens.
- Causal 3-D convolution pads k_t-1 frames before the input only, so frame 0 is encoded alone. That gives one tokenizer for both images and video.
- UCF-101 FVD 96.33 versus 107.15 for MAGVIT.
- VideoPoet (Kondratyuk, 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14125) [S] uses it frozen, alongside SoundStream audio tokens, with vocabulary 256 special + 262,144 visual + 4,096 audio.

Cosmos tokenizer (NVIDIA, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03575):
- [C] README: spatial 8× or 16×, temporal 4× or 8×, up to 2048× total. DV4x8x8 turns 9 frames at 512² into indices of shape (3, 64, 64); the causal first frame is kept separate.
- [S] Encoder begins with a 2-level Haar wavelet.

Emu3 (Wang, 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18869) [S]: 4×8×8 compression with a 32,768-entry codebook; a 4×512×512 clip becomes 4096 tokens.

Tokens per second at this project's scale (my arithmetic, causal 4× temporal, first frame separate):
- 64×64 at 8 fps with 8× spatial: 64 tokens per latent frame, i.e. 128 tokens/s. One 128-token window is about 1 s (about 8 frames).
- Same with 16× spatial: 16 tokens per latent frame, i.e. 32 tokens/s, 4 s per window.
- 32×32 at 8 fps with 8× spatial: also 32 tokens/s.
- 128×128 at 8 fps with 8× spatial: 512 tokens/s, i.e. 4 windows per second of video. Too costly given the throughput limit.

=== 5. SMALLEST STABLE CONFIGURATIONS AND COMPUTE ===

Published codecs train at GPU scale:
- DAC: about 3k hours of audio seen.
- EnCodec: about 10.7k hours.
- Mimi: about 4M × 128 × 12 s ≈ 1.7M hours.

My CPU runs saw about 2.3 hours of audio and reached envelope-level (not phase-level) reconstruction.

I found no primary source giving a "minimum stable" codec configuration. Minute-scale CPU training is enough to pick the frame rate, vocabulary and anti-collapse method. It is not enough to reach waveform fidelity. That needs the GPU (about 100k+ steps; unverified extrapolation).

=== 6. CODEC TRAINING vs LM TRAINING ===

Frozen after pretraining is the norm: AudioLM, MusicGen, VideoPoet and Chameleon all train the tokenizer first, then freeze it. For Emu3, the search extract only says its tokenizer was trained separately (end to end on image/video data) [S]; whether it was then frozen is (unverified).

Naive joint training fails:
- The argmax index is non-differentiable, and the STE path is unstable and collapses the codebook [S, search extract of end-to-end AR tokenizer work].
- REPA-E (Leng, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10483) [S]: back-propagating the generator loss into a VAE collapses the latent to simpler representations. Joint training only works with an added representation-alignment loss.
- ETT, end-to-end vision tokenizer tuning (Wang, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10562) [S] tunes the tokenizer through the codebook embeddings rather than the indices.

For continual learning, codec drift is itself a source of forgetting:
- Online continual compression, AQM (Caccia, 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.08019) [S]: old codes must stay decodable by later decoders. They use codebook freezing plus self-replay.
- The Discrete Audio Tokens survey (Mousavi, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10274) [S] classifies codec training as separate versus joint.

=== 7. SYNTHETIC DATA AND FORGETTING BENCHMARKS ===

Video and images:
- Moving MNIST (Srivastava, 2015, https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.04681) [S]: 2 digits in 64×64, 20 frames, bouncing off the walls.
- Captioned Bouncing MNIST, Sync-DRAW (Mittal, 2016, https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.10314) [S]: 12k GIFs of 16 frames with captions like "digit 0 is moving left and right".
- dSprites (Matthey, 2017, https://github.com/google-deepmind/dsprites-dataset) [S]: 737,280 64×64 images spanning 6 exhaustive latent factors.
- CLEVR (Johnson, 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.06890) [S].
- CLEVRER (Yi, 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.01442) [S]: 20k synthetic 5-second collision videos with more than 300k descriptive, explanatory, predictive and counterfactual QA pairs.
- CATER (Girdhar, 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.04744) [S]: 5.5k synthetic videos, 300 frames each.

Audio:
- CLEAR (Abdelnour, 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.10561) [S]: CLEVR-style acoustic QA over composed notes, with generation code.
- DAQA (Fayek, 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.09655) [S]: temporal-reasoning audio QA. Note that it uses real sound events.
- NSynth (Engel, 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.01279) [S]: 300k 4-second 16 kHz notes labelled with pitch, velocity and instrument. This is real audio, useful later for the same slots.
- Klatt formant synthesis (Klatt, 1980, JASA) [S]: the reference design for procedural vowels and syllables.

Measuring forgetting:
- Accuracy matrix R_ij with ACC, BWT and FWT (Lopez-Paz, 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.08840) [S].
- CLiMB (Srinivasan, 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.09059) [S]: continual-learning methods reduce multimodal forgetting but give no transfer.
- Hidden forgetting (Chen, 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02020) [S]: answer accuracy can survive while grounding shifts to other evidence channels. So measure grounding directly, not only the loss.

The tree already has most of the scheduling pieces:
- DATA_PHASE_SCHED (explicit phases).
- EVAL_HOLDOUT_WINDOWS (the retention probe behind the R matrix).
- forgetting_of and bwt_of in docs/04_CONTRACT.md.
- TOK_FREEZE_AT: the text analogue of freezing a codec.
codec.recommendations:
1. Audio package (AUD, following Proposal 01's one-package-per-modality shape). Codec: SEANet conv encoder/decoder, FSQ levels 8,5,5,5 (1000 codes, 10 bits) at 50 Hz. Add the per-dimension marginal-entropy bonus as a declared lever; it was the only thing that stopped collapse in my runs.
- 50 tokens/s puts 2.56 s of audio in one LM_CTX=128 window. It also fits inside LM_VOCAB_SLOTS=4096 alongside text.
- 25 Hz (5.1 s per window) is viable only with the entropy bonus; it lost 0.07 mel against 50 Hz.
- Log codes_used, perplexity and entropy bits as did-it-fire style counters from the first step: collapse is silent and happened in 7 of 15 runs. When it happens mel sits near 1.12, and the loss curve alone did not flag it in my runs.
- Keep RVQ as an arm, with EMA, k-means init and a real dead-code threshold (EnCodec uses an EMA count below 2). Flattened RVQ costs 4× the sequence length, so if it is used, use the MusicGen delay pattern with one head per level rather than flattening.

2. Train the codec as a separate phase and freeze it. Pretrain on synthetic data on the GPU with GAN or feature-matching losses and quantizer dropout, then freeze and version it.
- Minute-scale CPU runs only fit the spectral envelope (SI-SNR stays near -45 dB), so fidelity is a GPU job. Budget 100k-400k steps (DAC 400k; unverified for this size).
- Do not back-propagate the LM loss into the codebook. REPA-E, the STE-collapse evidence and AQM all argue against it.
- Treat codec weights and FSQ levels as a checkpointed quantity with a save path, a restore path and a geometry rule. Changing levels or frame rate is a new token space and must refuse to load old LM rows.
- A codec retrained later on real data is a new version. Re-tokenise stored memory entries, or keep the old version for old areas; otherwise codec drift shows up as forgetting in the LM (AQM).

3. Video package (VID): causal 3-D conv tokenizer (MAGVIT-v2 / Cosmos style) with FSQ plus the same entropy bonus, 4× temporal, first frame separate so images and video share one tokenizer.
- Start at 64×64, 8 fps, 16× spatial (32 tokens/s, 4 s per window).
- Or 32×32 with 8× spatial (also 32 tokens/s).
- Only move to 64×64 with 8× spatial (128 tokens/s, about 1 s per window) once the throughput problem is profiled. Media cost enters through windows per media-second; window length stays 128 tokens.

4. Output head. FSQ allows factorised output heads: 8+5+5+5 = 23 logits instead of 1000 (unverified that this beats a joint head). That keeps vocab-slot pressure off the text BPE and is cheap to A/B. Decide M5 (joint or per-modality vocabulary) with this option on the table.

5. Synthetic generators. Every sample carries its generating parameters, and the paired text is rendered from those same parameters by templates. Held-out sets come from disjoint seeds, and some attribute combinations are held out to test composition.
- Audio: tones, chirps (direction and rate), AM/FM, harmonic complexes, Klatt-style vowels and syllables, scale melodies, beep counts and rhythms. My generator in codec.py (the functions tone, chirp, harmonic, syllables, melody) is a starting point.
- Video: dSprites-factor shapes, bouncing and colliding 2-D physics (CLEVRER-like but 2-D and cheap), glyph digits drawn procedurally rather than taken from MNIST.
- Audio-video pairs: a collision emits a click, shape maps to pitch. These give WORLD a physics forecasting target and give grounding checks in both directions.

6. Forgetting protocol. Use explicit DATA_PHASE_SCHED phases, one area per modality or task family, for example "text|aud_tones|aud_vowels|vid_bounce|text".
- Evaluate every area's fixed procedural held-out set at every phase boundary to fill the R matrix; report ACC, BWT and FWT.
- Add a joint i.i.d. upper-bound arm and a fine-tune-only lower-bound arm.
- Measure grounding separately from loss: attribute accuracy for text given media and media given text, so hidden forgetting shows up.
- Mark phase switches in Windows. Give media Windows their own clock kind, or add a named conversion in spine.derive (M1).

7. Throughput. Pre-tokenise the synthetic corpus offline with the frozen codec. It runs about 40-50× faster than real time on one CPU thread at 0.65M params, so the LM loop only sees token ids and per-window cost stays that of a 128-token window.

designs.route: Route 1: one shared discrete token stream (early fusion). Learned from-scratch FSQ codecs (AUD now, VID next) emit ids into the one sequence the LM already predicts. The ids sit at a FIXED ABSOLUTE media id base, in LM row tables separate from the text rows. One softmax over the concatenated rows, masked per position by modality. Paired caption<->clip areas give understanding (clip -> caption) and generation (caption -> clip) as next-token prediction. Media areas are ordinary DATA areas, so DOM, FAB, MEM and the goal-B phase protocol treat them like text areas, with a hard modality gate at the top of DOM.
designs.summary:
Recommendation: build Route 1 with five pinned decisions.
(1) Media ids live at derive.MEDIA_ID_BASE = 2^20 plus a fixed per-modality block. They are never inside [0, LM_VOCAB_SLOTS), so the MAY_WIDEN prefix rule, BPE minting, CAP's vocab arm and every stored id stay valid when text widens or a modality is added.
(2) LM gets separate media row tables, and decode takes a per-position modality mask.
(3) There is ONE Windows clock kind (M1). Every window is still LM_CTX ids of one sequence. Per-modality content goes into readings (bits per codec token, bits per audio second), not into clocks.
(4) The codec trains inside the loop during a codec phase, then freezes (AUD_TRAIN_WINDOWS) before any audio enters the LM stream. The LM loss never back-propagates into the codec.
(5) Paired areas use output-segment-only loss, and a new modality is added with the rehearsed protocol (text stays in the phase).

Measured on CPU with the tree's own GRU LM (width 128, ctx 128, vocab_slots 4096), the tree's own WORLD, tree-TOK text ids and a learned FSQ audio codec. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/mm/design-stream/.
- Sharing the model costs text almost nothing per text window: 2.748 bits/token at 8k text windows in the joint run, against 2.755 text-only. It does cost wall time.
- Adding audio with no replay forgets text: +0.230 bits/token (+7.8%), and WORLD's text prediction error triples (1.02 -> 3.21). A 30% text replay removes both: text 2.966 -> 2.906, still improving; WORLD 1.10.
- 25 Hz codes beat 50 Hz for the LM even though that codec is worse.
- Output-only loss doubles understanding at 50 Hz (14% -> 28% exact caption).

What measures badly:
- Understanding reaches 34-41% exact caption. Chance is 6.25%. A dedicated classifier on the same codes gets 73-80%.
- Generation is the weakest part: 20-41% attribute recovery on 25 Hz generations against a 58% codec ceiling, and 19-28% at 50 Hz against 76%.
- The codec reproduces spectral envelopes, not phase (SNR about 0 dB).
- All of this is one seed at CPU budgets of 8k-24k windows, so these are shape findings, not verdicts.
designs.architecture:
DATA FLOW PER EPOCH (build time and after a codec freeze):
1. DATA.draw_stream returns a Stream whose text bytes are exactly today's. It gains a typed media track: MediaSegment(at_byte, modality, area, clip_key, n_units). A paired example is a text caption plus a media clip, in caption-first (generation) or clip-first (understanding) order.
2. TOK.tokenize segments the TEXT bytes only.
   - bytes_per_token is measured only on the build heads of text areas. This closes the 9% signature-width shrink the map measured (risk 1).
3. AUD.encode(frozen codec) turns each clip into offsets in [0, codebook).
4. New TOK.interleave(tok, seg, media) merges the two into ONE Segmentation(ids, byte_pos, labels, bytes_per_token, unit_pos, modality).
   - A media clip becomes [OPEN] + codes + [CLOSE], all as absolute ids MEDIA_ID_BASE + block(k) + offset.
   - byte_pos keeps the TRUE byte offset for text. For media tokens it holds the insertion offset.
   - unit_pos is a strictly increasing stream coordinate: text byte = 1 unit, media token = 1 unit. It equals byte_pos exactly when there is no media.
   - modality is 0 for text, 1 for aud, 2 for vid. OPEN is predicted in text context; codes and CLOSE are in media context.
5. Windows are cut exactly as today (x = ids[a:a+ctx], y = ids[a+1:b]), so windows_in_epoch = (len(ids)-1)//ctx counts media automatically.

PER FLUSH:
1. LM.embed maps ids to rows through derive.token_row(ids, text_rows, media_spans), which is one torch.where.
   - Text ids < vocab_slots index emb.
   - Media ids index media_emb[k].
2. WORLD.forecast(obs_emb) goes into LM.encode(extra=), unchanged (None at WORLD_FEEDBACK=0).
3. FAB.forward(head=...), where the root binds head per flush as `lambda h: LM.decode(..., modality=seg.modality[y])`.
4. LM.decode concatenates [head(h), media_head_k(h)...] and applies the allowed-row mask:
   - text positions: live text rows plus OPEN;
   - aud positions: aud codes plus CLOSE.
5. The loss is LM.lm_loss(logits, y, weights=w), where w = role weight x modality weight:
   - role: 0 on the prompt segment of a paired example, 1 on its output;
   - modality: AUD_LOSS_W, VID_LOSS_W.
6. + WORLD.loss_terms(obs_emb, valid=same-modality pairs).
7. + AUD.loss_terms(raw clips), during the codec phase only, on its own OPT 'codec' group.
8. MEM.write gets positions = unit_pos. SIG runs in space='tokens' over the joint row alphabet.
9. DOM.observe(..., modality=class of the window's majority label). This is a hard top level: centroid search, spawn and merge happen only within a class (Proposal 02's modality-top/content-leaf, using the modality we know exactly rather than a learned one).

ID LAYOUT (spine/derive.py, known-answer table in tests/test_derive.py):
- MEDIA_ID_BASE = 1<<20. media_id_base(k) = MEDIA_ID_BASE + k*(1<<16), with k fixed per package forever: AUD=0, VID=1, IMG=2 reserved.
- Inside a block: [0, codebook) codes, then OPEN and CLOSE. The span is prod(levels)+2, i.e. 1002 for FSQ 8,5,5,5.
- Row mapping is ephemeral (per forward only). Everything persisted (MEM entries, DOM histograms, checkpoints, eval samples) stores absolute ids. So widening vocab_slots moves nothing, and adding VID moves nothing of AUD.

GENERATION GRAMMAR: after OPEN, exactly F = clip_s x frame_rate codes, then CLOSE. The sampler's mode_fn is built from that rule.
designs.codecs:
AUD codec (new package AUD):
- Architecture: SEANet-style 1-D conv encoder/decoder (ELU, C=16, latent 64, about 0.65M params).
- Quantizer: FSQ levels 8,5,5,5 (1000 codes, GroupNorm pre-projection), plus a per-dimension marginal-entropy bonus (AUD_ENT_W=0.1). The bonus is what prevented collapse in the codec research runs, where plain FSQ collapsed in 3 of 5.
- Loss: multi-scale log-mel + multi-scale STFT + L1. No GAN; that is a later GPU arm together with quantizer dropout.

Default frame rate: 25 Hz at 8 kHz (hop 320). 50 Hz is the A/B arm. Reason: the LM learned 25 Hz codes better at every budget measured (understanding 41% vs 28% at 8k windows; generation probe up to 41% vs 28%). This holds even though the 25 Hz codec is worse on reconstruction:
- mel 1.03 vs 0.99 on 128 held-out clips (silence = 1.81);
- 109 vs 237 codes used;
- probe on reconstructions 58% vs 76%.
The owner should re-decide at GPU scale, because codec quality there is a GPU-step question.

Training inside the framework, in a codec phase:
- For the first AUD_TRAIN_WINDOWS windows, AUD.loss_terms runs once per flush on AUD_BATCH raw clips of AUD_CROP_S seconds. DATA.media_batch supplies them from audio areas on rng child aud.train.
- Meanwhile the LM trains on text only; audio areas are phase-gated out.
- At the freeze (a Gate, on Cadences.due with a Windows period), the collapse check runs (codes_used >= AUD_COLLAPSE_MIN, else the Gate reports and the freeze is refused and extended once).
- Then the root re-encodes every media segment and rebuilds the Segmentation through TOK.interleave, the same event shape as TOK's retok_pending.
- The LM loss never flows into the codec: codes are integer ids and REPA-E-style collapse is avoided.

Versioning: AUD_VERSION is an EXACT geometry field.
- A later retrain (for example on real audio) is a new version. It either keeps the old block for old areas, or goes to a new block k with rows initialised from nearest old-code rows (the analogue of LM_NEW_ROW_INIT).
- A codec never changes under a trained LM silently.

Offline cost: 0.011-0.015 s CPU per audio-second to encode (66-90x real time, 1 thread). Decoding costs about the same.

VID codec (new package VID, stage 7):
- Causal 3-D conv tokenizer, first frame separate, same FSQ + entropy bonus.
- 32x32 at 8 fps, 4x temporal and 8x spatial compression, giving 16 tokens per latent frame = 32 tokens/s, 4 s per 128-id window.
- 64x64 with 8x spatial (128 tokens/s) only after the throughput profile.

Rejected for the default: flattened RVQ 4x256 (200 tokens/s, 0.64 s per window). If RVQ is ever used, use the delay pattern.
designs.synthetic_data:
Generators are owned by DATA, because the corpus is DATA's and real data later goes into the same Areas slots.
- Selected by DATA_MEDIA_AREAS (default "" = off, so the tree stays bit-identical). Example: "aud/tones:pair,aud/beeps:pair,aud/vowels:pair".
- Each area is seeded per child data.synth.<label>. The held-out split uses child data.holdout.<label>, DATA_SYNTH_HOLDOUT=0.1.
- This fixes the "synthetic holds nothing out" gap; without it the goal-B R matrix cannot be measured.

Every clip carries its generating parameters. The caption is rendered from the discrete ones by template; continuous ones (exact frequency, f0, gain, noise) add variety.

Prototype generator (audgen.py): 8 kHz, 1 s clips, 16 caption classes in 5 families:
- tone low/mid/high;
- chirp up/down;
- 2/3/4 beeps low/high;
- vowel a/i/u (formant harmonic synthesis);
- notes rising/falling (4 scale notes).

Pairing: DATA_PAIR_CAPTION_FIRST=0.5 is the fraction of examples laid out caption-first (generation) rather than clip-first (understanding).
- The loss applies to the output segment only (VideoPoet-style). Measured: understanding 14% -> 28% at 50 Hz. The price is higher caption bits in the generation direction, where the caption is now an unweighted prompt.

Composition probe: DATA_SYNTH_HOLD_COMBOS lists attribute combinations never drawn in training (for example "3 beeps low"). It gives a zero-shot understand/generate check.

Exact scoring:
- DATA.recover(dat, clips, area) is an ANALYTIC parameter estimator per family: dominant-frequency band, onset count, spectral-centroid slope, formant ratio, per-quarter pitch trend. It needs no training and cannot drift.
- A learned probe is secondary only. It is fragile: my first probe, trained on clean clips, scored codec reconstructions at 2.3%. A probe retrained on noisy clips plus reconstructions scored 99.2% on real clips, 76%/58% on 50/25 Hz reconstructions, and 6-11% on random codes.

Video (stage 7): dSprites-factor shapes, bouncing/colliding 2-D balls, procedural glyph digits, with captions from the same parameters. Audio-video pairs: a collision emits a click, and shape maps to pitch. These give WORLD a physics target and give grounding checks in both directions.
