designs.continual_learning:
A modality is an AREA, and adding one is the existing goal-B add-an-area protocol (Q-DATA-7). Example: DATA_PHASE_SCHED "eng,py,num,c|eng,py,num,c|eng,py,num,c,aud/tones|...,aud/vowels".

Measured (tree GRU+WORLD, 4k text windows, then 4k windows of audio phase):
- Pure-add (audio only in phase 2): text held-out 2.966 -> 3.196 bits/token (+7.8%, BWT negative). WORLD's forward-prediction MSE on text rose 1.02 -> 3.21, so WORLD forgets harder than the LM.
- Rehearsed (70% audio / 30% text): text 2.966 -> 2.906 (still improving) and WORLD text 1.10. Audio cost was small: 3.03 vs 2.96 bits/code.
- So the default for adding a modality is REHEARSED; pure-add stays the named comparison arm. This matches the tree's existing phase_sched default, which is rehearsed.

Joint capacity at width 128 is not the constraint:
- the joint model at 8k text windows (16k total) had text 2.748 vs 2.755 text-only;
- at 10k text windows it had 2.707.
Caveat: one seed, and the lr schedules differ.

DOM: a hard class gate (text / aud-paired / vid-paired), so a media window can never be assigned to a text domain and vice versa. Measure M2 first: train SIG on the mixed stream and report the modality purity of flat domains. If flat is pure, the gate is a no-op.

FAB: breadth cap and cull are computed within a class. Expert specialisation by modality is expected (MoMa/LIMoE). Hard expert groups vs learned routing is an A/B.

MEM: per-class floor (capacity x src_share / n_classes / live sources in class). Retrieval over codec ids is a real next-token distribution. Positions are unit_pos.

Forgetting measurement: the R matrix runs over every area at every phase boundary, on the synthetic held-out sets, with ACC/BWT/FWT from the existing forgetting_of/bwt_of. Per area it records:
- text: bits/byte;
- audio: bits per codec token AND bits per audio second, caption exact-match accuracy (understanding), analytic attribute recovery of generated clips (generation), codec mel;
- WORLD forward MSE per area.
Grounding is measured separately from loss (hidden-forgetting warning): wrong-caption bits minus right-caption bits per clip, i.e. how much the caption informs the codes. Measured 4.9-13 bits per clip; log2(16) = 4.

Codec drift: frozen codec versions. A new version is a new block (or a remap with row init). No silent retraining under a trained LM.

Arms:
- zero-init tanh gate / lr-shield of text rows (Flamingo/LMFusion pattern, via the existing OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM);
- generative self-replay of old audio;
- learning-rate re-warm at the boundary.
designs.generation:
Generation is next-token sampling through the LM head:
- the prompt is caption + OPEN;
- sample exactly F codes from the modality-masked distribution (grammar from TOK.interleave's rule);
- CLOSE;
- AUD.decode turns the codes into a waveform.
Understanding is greedy text after OPEN codes CLOSE, masked to text rows, stopping at "." or an OPEN. Continuation (half a clip -> the rest) and cross-modal chains (text -> audio -> text) use the same sampler.

Build the TEXT sampler first (EVAL.generate plus the whole-path logits_fn, stage 2), as Proposal 01 says. Media sampling is then the same function with a mode_fn. Hidden-state caching for the GRU arm, and KV caching for the transformer arm, belong in the sampler. My uncached prototype took 0.04-0.10 s per 1 s clip on CPU.

Evaluation (EVAL.media_scores on fixed held-out prompts under frozen_rng, every curve period), measured values:

| Metric | Measured |
|---|---|
| Codec ceiling (probe on reconstructions of real clips) | 58% (25 Hz), 76% (50 Hz) |
| Code-space classifier ceiling | 73-80% |
| Generation, probe recovery | 25 Hz / 20k windows: 22-41% by temperature, best 0.3-0; 50 Hz / 20k: 19-28% |
| Generation, code-space classifier | 23-40% |
| Generation, family accuracy | up to 81% (greedy, 25 Hz) |
| Understanding, exact caption | 34-41% at 25 Hz; 28-34% at 50 Hz (output-only loss) |
| Code bits given caption | 2.19 bits/code = 55 bits/s (25 Hz, 20k); 2.72 = 136 bits/s (50 Hz) |

- Generation is scored by DATA.recover (analytic, primary) and by the secondary probe; accuracy of the attribute the prompt named is the number to watch. Chance is 6.25%.
- Understanding: exact caption match and per-attribute accuracy.
- Likelihood uses exact bits because codes are discrete. That is the reason discrete was chosen over a continuous head for M3.

The Transfusion/GIVT continuous head over codec latents is a later arm, judged on generation per FLOP.
designs.world_model_role:
WORLD is included with ZERO new WORLD code on the discrete path. It reads obs_emb = LM.embed(x), and codec ids are rows in LM's embedding. This cashes world/api.py's own claim that "a second sense needs new rows in LM's embedding and nothing new here".

Measured with the tree's WORLD (lat 32, VICReg, horizon 1) trained jointly:
- forward-prediction MSE on text latents stays about 1.0 (no better than the unit variance);
- on audio-code latents it falls to 0.54-0.69.
So WORLD finds real forward structure in audio that it does not find in text (not yet compared to a persistence baseline). In pure-add it forgot text 3x, and rehearsal contained that.

Design additions:
(1) WORLD.loss_terms(valid=) drops (t, t+h) pairs that cross a modality boundary. Today horizon-1 pairs straddle caption/code boundaries in every paired window.
(2) WORLD_MEDIA_HORIZON (tokens) sets the horizon on media positions. At 25 Hz, h = 1 is 40 ms ahead; h = 5 is 200 ms.
(3) WORLD_FEEDBACK stays False. The owner's GPU experiment should re-test feedback on paired-audio areas, where WORLD has more to predict than on text (Q-WORLD-10 was text).
(4) Hybrid arm: AUD.obs projects the codec's continuous pre-quantisation latent, through a zero-born AUD-owned Linear, into obs_emb (added before WORLD). WORLD then sees continuous frames while the LM still sees codes. No LM input-contract change.
(5) Later arm: WORLD's latent forecast feeds an auxiliary next-code prediction (Genie-style dynamics) or a Diffusion-Forcing head.
(6) WORLD metrics go into the R matrix per area. Its per-position memoryless predictor is a known limit for video.

designs.risks:
Ranked:
1. Generation quality. It is the weakest measured piece (at best 41% vs a 58% codec ceiling) and improves slowly with windows. Mitigations to A/B: 25 Hz or lower; output-only loss; low-temperature sampling; more audio windows on GPU; a factorised FSQ head (8+5+5+5 logits); a continuous GIVT/MAR head arm.
2. Codec fidelity. Phase is not learned (SNR about 0 dB), and 50 Hz codes are harder for the LM. It needs GPU steps plus adversarial/feature losses. The owner must accept an envelope-level codec on synthetic data first.
3. Forgetting on pure-add (+7.8% text, 3x WORLD). Rehearsal must be the default protocol. WORLD forgetting has to be reported per area or it hides.
4. Signature/DOM (M2) is unmeasured on mixed windows. Paired windows mix caption and codes, so the class gate uses the area's declared class, not a learned one.
5. Mask defect. mask_dead_rows' suffix mask (lm/api.py decode, dead[live_vocab:]) would -inf media rows if rows are laid out naively. Fixed by restricting the dead mask to text rows; this needs a test.
6. The bpt/signature-width shift if media or captions leak into TOK's build corpus. Text-only build heads remove it; a test must assert build bpt is unchanged when media is on.
7. Checkpoint and resume: new tensors and new manifest fields break every text checkpoint without the absent-field ruling and the add_param_group path.
8. MEM floor dilution and FAB breadth denominators: handled per class, but that changes the text-side numbers when media is on (never when off).
9. Loss balance: the per-window loss mixes units (bits per code vs bits per text token). DOM competence, FAB comp_ema and OPT best_bpb must read per-modality numbers or they compare incomparable values (M3). Use the per-area R matrix, never a pooled loss.
10. Codec collapse is silent (3 of 5 plain-FSQ runs in the research runs). Hence the entropy bonus plus the collapse Gate before freeze.
11. Codec drift if anyone retrains a codec under a trained LM. Versions are EXACT geometry.
12. Throughput: per-window cost is flat, but media multiplies window counts. The late-run GPU slowdown makes hours of audio expensive.
13. Evidence quality: one seed, small n, CPU contention, a simplified optimizer, and no FAB/MEM/DOM in the prototype loop. Shared vs masked softmax differ within noise on likelihood; the mask's case rests on grammar violations (116 vs 185) and on the ID-layout requirement.
designs.rejected_alternatives:
- Codec ids serialised as bytes through BPE. Greedy longest-match and mint_burst would merge codes with text (map risk 2).
- Codec block inside [0, vocab_slots): at the top it moves when vocab_slots widens (MAY_WIDEN); at 256 it collides with minted rows of existing checkpoints. The prototype used an in-table block at 3072 only for speed; mathematically it is the same as separate tables with concatenated logits.
- Remapping media rows with OPT.remap_rows whenever vocab_slots widens. Every stored id in MEM and DOM would need rewriting.
- Split clock kinds per modality (M1). Under one stream every window is ctx ids, so splitting multiplies cadence levers for no type-safety gain. Per-modality readings carry the content difference.
- Flattened RVQ 4x256: 200 tok/s, 0.64 s per window, and no reconstruction gain from levels 2-4 in the research runs.
- Plain FSQ without the entropy bonus: it collapsed.
- Joint codec+LM backprop through the codes: STE/REPA-E collapse evidence, and it makes token meaning drift under the LM.
- Unmasked shared softmax as the default: equal likelihood, 1.6x more grammar violations, text ids can appear inside clips, and it keeps codec rows in every text denominator.
- Continuous media through LM.encode(extra=): post-trunk, so it never passes the GRU/attention (Route 2's problem). Kept only as the WORLD hybrid obs arm.
- One MEDIA package: it violates Proposal 01's one-package-per-modality census shape. The FSQ duplication between AUD and VID is about 40 lines, guarded by a twin test.
- Learned probe as the only generation metric: fragile (2.3% on reconstructions before augmentation). Analytic recovery is primary.
- A flat 64-d signature with no class gate: unmeasured (M2), and Proposal 01 predicts it collapses onto modality.

designs.route: ROUTE 2, design-world: continuous latents through WORLD. Learned, causal per-modality codecs (new packages AUD and VID) turn media into continuous latent frames. Those latents enter WORLD as observations through a per-source encoder in one shared latent space; this is the obs_emb plug. The LM is conditioned on WORLD's latent state: K pooled latent embeddings are inserted into the LM input sequence at the clip's anchor and pass through the trunk. Generation runs WORLD forward from the LM's hidden state at the end of a caption (text to audio) or from an audio prompt (continuation). AUD then maps WORLD latents back to codec latents and decodes them. TOK, MEM and SIG stay text-only. Media never enters Stream.bytes; each clip is anchored to a byte offset of its caption. Three things are required, because without each of them this route measured badly: WORLD needs temporal context (a new WORLD_CTX='gru' arm), WORLD needs a free-running rollout loss, and the LM needs an input-side insert path (LM.encode(media=)).
designs.summary:
I prototyped the riskiest piece, audio through WORLD, on CPU in about 25 minutes of total compute. The prototype used the REAL src/world/api.py (a scratch copy) as the baseline arm and a learned-from-scratch causal audio codec on synthetic captioned melodies. Everything is single-seed and small-scale.

What held:
- Codec. A 312k-parameter causal conv codec (log-mel in and out, 32-d continuous latent at 25 Hz) trained in 125 s. Log-mel L1 is 0.433, against 1.706 for a mean-spectrogram decoder. A parameter-recovery probe recovers 100% of notes and timbre from the reconstructions.
- Understanding. Inserting K=8 pooled WORLD-latent embeddings through the LM trunk cut caption cost from 9.7 to 0.37 bits per caption (1.00 to 0.039 bits/byte). Exact captions reached 0.94 and note accuracy 0.978. WORLD's latent was a better LM input than raw codec latents (0.817 exact).
- Text-to-audio generation through WORLD with a GRU context and a free-running loss is perfect on held-out captions: all four notes plus timbre correct in 100% of clips, L1 0.272. The same generator without WORLD reached 0.875 and L1 0.645.

What failed, and forces the design:
- The current memoryless WORLD cannot generate. Its rollout diverged (log-mel L1 6.8 on held-out, 84 on the compositional set), and notes 2-4 were at chance.
- Teacher-forced training alone fails for every arm. Notes 2-4 were at chance (about 0.1), because errors compound once the model runs on its own predictions.
- The existing post-trunk hook LM.encode(extra=) reaches only 0.485 note accuracy pooled. With position-query attention, which still fits the current signature, it reaches 0.80.
- My mixture-density (GMM) sampling heads were worse than the deterministic arm (0.54-0.64 legal against 0.99). This route therefore has no validated stochastic sampler yet.
- Compositional generalisation is poor everywhere. On held-out timbre x first-note combinations, understanding note accuracy was 0.21-0.40, and generation got the first note wrong in every clip (0.0).
- WORLD's own one-step reading, inv against persistence, points the wrong way for generation. The best one-step arm (0.19x persistence) is poor at rollout (note 4 grammar-legal only 0.34). The arm with the free-running loss scores 0.83x yet gets 0.97.

Cost: one 2.56 s clip adds 8 inserted positions to a 128-token window (1.06x sequence), and about 50 ms of CPU time per media-bearing window (about +18% of the 275 ms real window). About 35 ms of that is the 64-step free-running rollout, which a cadence lever reduces.

Scale of change: two new packages (AUD now, VID later), 4 frozen signatures move, about 17 new entry points for audio (137 to 154), no new cross-package wires, one new clock kind (Frames).

designs.architecture:
DATA FLOW PER FLUSH (media-bearing window; text-only windows are unchanged)
1. DATA.draw_stream yields Stream.bytes exactly as today, plus Stream.media: a tuple of MediaSegment(modality, area, anchor_byte, payload_ref, params, task).
   - task is 'understand' (the clip is anchored at the caption start and the caption follows) or 'generate' (the clip is anchored at the caption end and is the target).
   - Captions are ordinary text bytes inside Stream.bytes. The clip payload never is.
2. A compose join, _media_for_window(stream, seg, a, b), maps each anchor to a token index with the searchsorted of Segmentation.byte_pos. The insert goes before the first token whose byte_pos >= anchor, so a token straddling the anchor does not see the clip. DATA spaces anchors at least DATA_MEDIA_EVERY bytes apart, which gives at most one clip per window.
3. AUD.encode(aud, codec, frames) turns log-mel (B, 64, 128) into a codec latent m (B, 64, 32), causal, at 25 Hz. It runs under no_grad after the codec phase freezes. Offline pre-encoding is an allowed optimisation.
4. obs = AUD.to_obs(m), shape (B, 64, LM.width). Then WORLD.loss_terms(world, w, obs, source='aud'):
   - a per-source encoder produces z (B, 64, WORLD.lat), in the latent space shared with text;
   - a causal context GRU (WORLD_CTX='gru') feeds the per-source predictor pool;
   - the existing predict_w / collapse_w terms apply.
   Text still calls loss_terms(..., source='text') on LM.embed(x), bit-identical at WORLD_CTX='none'.
5. Understanding. AUD.to_lm(aud, codec, z) pools z into K=8 embeddings plus AUD's own positional rows. Then LM.encode(lm, model, x, extra=..., media=(emb, at)) splices them into the embedding sequence at token index `at`, runs the trunk over L+K positions, and returns h for the L text positions only. So FAB, MEM, decode and loss shapes do not change. Text pos rows are unchanged, and pos_max stays EXACT.
6. Generation (task='generate'). cond = h[:, at-1], the LM hidden state at the caption's last byte. Then:
   - WORLD.rollout(world, w, cond=cond, prompt=None, steps=AUD_GEN_LEN, source='aud', grad=True) returns z_roll;
   - AUD.loss_terms(..., z_roll=z_roll, target=m) applies gen_w * MSE(from_world(z_roll), m). This is the free-running loss; it is due every AUD_GEN_EVERY flushes through Cadences.due.
   - Continuation uses prompt=z[:, :32] and cond=None.
7. The total at loop.py:1871 gains world_aud_loss, aud_recon (codec phase only), aud_readout and aud_gen. All four join the non-finite blame list.

PACKAGE OWNERSHIP
- AUD (new) owns the codec, to_obs, to_lm, from_world, the readout/gen/recon losses, and the codec version and freeze.
- WORLD owns per-source encoders, the context model, per-source predictor pools and rollout.
- LM owns the insert path.
- DATA owns the synthetic generators, holdout and media segments.
- EVAL owns the parameter-recovery probe and the media generation metric.
- No package imports another. LM.width and WORLD.lat reach AUD as build arguments, following the open_store(key_dim=LM.width) idiom, so no wire budget is spent.

VIDEO (VID, stage 7, same shape)
- Frames: 32x32x3 at 8 fps.
- Encoder: causal 3-D conv, 2x temporal and 8x spatial, giving a 4x4x8 = 128-d latent frame at 4 Hz.
- to_obs(128 -> LM.width); from_world(WORLD.lat -> 128); insert K=8.
- WORLD.lat 32 is too small for video (the map predicted this). WORLD_LAT rises to 64 when VID is on; lat is EXACT geometry, so that is a new-run decision.

TEXT PATH AT DEFAULTS
With DATA_MEDIA='none', AUD_ENABLED=0, VID_ENABLED=0 and WORLD_CTX='none', no new row fires. Every new call returns its null answer (the D4 pattern), and the seed-0 loss curve must be bit-identical to d97779d.
designs.codecs:
AUD CODEC (prototype-measured shape)
- Frontend: fixed DSP, not learned and with no weights. 8 kHz, STFT 512, hop 160, 64 log-mel bins at 50 Hz.
- Encoder: causal Conv1d stack with dilations, 128 channels, one stride-2 layer, ending in tanh. Output is a 32-d latent at 25 Hz: 64 latent frames per 2.56 s clip.
- Decoder: causal mirror (upsample x2), outputs log-mel. During training it sees N(0, 0.05) noise on its input latent, so it tolerates WORLD's imperfect predictions.
- Size: 312,288 parameters. Loss: L1 on log-mel.
- CPU cost: encode 0.82 ms per 2.56 s clip; encode+decode RTF 0.00044 on one thread. Training fwd+bwd is 3.83 ms per clip.
- Waveform: a learned vocoder stage (AUD_VOCODER='none'|'conv') is SEPARATE and GPU-bound. The research-codecs agent measured a waveform SEANet reaching spectral envelope but not phase within 2k CPU steps (SI-SNR about -45 dB). My prototype stops at log-mel, which is enough for the parameter-recovery metrics.

NO QUANTISER
The route is continuous. That removes the collapse failure mode that took 7 of 15 discrete runs in the codec research. It gives up exact media likelihood (see risks).

ANTI-COLLAPSE
- The codec latent is anchored by reconstruction, with no collapse term inside AUD.
- WORLD's latent is anchored by VICReg (existing W_COV, collapse_w) plus the from_world readout MSE (readout_w).
- latent_std stayed 1.00-1.03 in every WORLD arm.
- Counters: aud.latent_std and world.source.aud.latent_std, gauges from the first flush.

TRAINING REGIME (AUD_TRAIN)
- 'phase', the default: the codec trains on recon only for the first AUD_FREEZE_AT windows of the first audio phase, then freezes and bumps its version. This follows the literature consensus and REPA-E.
- 'joint': an arm.
- 'frozen': loads only.
- WORLD, LM and gen losses never back-propagate into the codec encoder; the prototype kept it frozen from stage 2 on.
- AUD_VERSION is EXACT geometry. A retrained codec is a new version, and old areas either keep their version or are re-encoded (see continual_learning).

VID CODEC (stage 7, not prototyped)
- Causal 3-D conv (MAGVIT-v2 style: the first frame is encoded alone, so images and video share one encoder), 2x temporal, 8x spatial on 32x32 at 8 fps. The latent is 4x4x8 = 128-d per latent frame at 4 Hz.
- Loss: L1 plus a gradient-difference loss on frames.
- Same noise-robust decoder rule.
designs.synthetic_data:
PROTOTYPE GENERATOR (synth.py; to be ported into DATA as a synthetic media family)
- Audio: 8 kHz, 2.56 s clips of 4 notes, 0.64 s each.
- Pitch: 8 pitches at 220*1.25^k Hz. Each note has a 10 ms attack and an exponential decay (tau 0.35 s), so the latent encodes the phase within a note.
- Timbres: 3 (sine; harmonic 1, 1/2, 1/3; odd 1, 1/3, 1/5), random amplitude 0.3-0.8, noise floor 0.003.
- Melody: an order-2 Markov grammar per area. Each (n1, n2) pair has two successors with probability 0.7 / 0.3. Order-2 on purpose: it separates a memoryless WORLD from a context WORLD. The order-1-optimal legality for note 3 is 0.469; chance is 0.25.
- Captions render from the parameters, e.g. 'harm:cbbb.'. The Shannon floor is about 9.3 bits per caption, and the text-only LM measured 9.7.
- Cost: 1.3 ms per clip on one thread, so generating on the fly is cheaper than the LM step.
- Parameters travel with every sample.

HOLDOUT (fixes the data/api.py:455-457 "synthetic holds nothing out" gap)
- An in-distribution holdout drawn from the disjoint child stream data.holdout.<area> (400 clips).
- A compositional holdout: attribute combinations never trained (timbre 'odd' with first note a or b, 200 clips). This is the grounding and composition test.

DATA LEVERS (PREFIX DATA)
- media: 'none' | 'aud' | 'aud,vid'. Default 'none'.
- media_every: bytes between anchors, 4096.
- media_gen_frac: share of 'generate' tasks, 0.5.
- media_holdout: fraction, 0.1.
- media_compose_holdout: True.
- aud_kinds: 'melody,tone,chirp,syllable'. Tones, chirps, AM/FM and Klatt syllables come from the research-codecs generator.

AREAS
- Each media area is a DATA area named with the slash rule, e.g. 'aud/melody_g1', 'aud/melody_g2', 'aud/chirps', 'vid/bounce'.
- Seeded per child data.synth.<label>.
- An area differs by grammar seed, generator family or timbre set. That gives goal B a controllable distribution shift with exact labels.

LATER FAMILIES
- VID: bouncing and colliding 2-D sprites (dSprites factors: shape, colour, size, velocity), with procedurally drawn glyph digits.
- Paired AV: a collision emits a click, and shape maps to pitch. This gives WORLD a cross-modal forecasting target.

REAL DATA
Real data later enters the same MediaSegment slot, with params=None; probe metrics then fall back to recon and caption bits.

designs.continual_learning:
AREAS AND SCHEDULE (answers M10: yes)
- A modality or task family is a DATA area, e.g. DATA_PHASE_SCHED='eng|aud/melody_g1|aud/melody_g2|eng'.
- Plan.protocol (rehearsed or pure-add, Q-DATA-7) applies unchanged.
- Adding audio to a running text run is a resume under the NEW_PACKAGE geometry rule, with every new pathway born inert (zero-born to_obs, cond projection and WORLD source slice).

ISOLATION FIRST
1. WORLD: per-source predictor pools. An audio area can grow its own predictors under WORLD.manage, zero-born by the existing rule, without touching text's pool. Area-specific growth inside the audio pool is the MoMa pattern (hard modality groups, learned routing inside).
2. Codec: frozen per version after its phase, so old areas' latents keep their meaning (the AQM argument). A new codec version for real data either keeps the old version's weights for old areas (payload holds both), or re-encodes the holdout and replays through the new one. Chosen per arm and measured.
3. LM: media enters only through inserted positions, so text-only windows run the unchanged trunk. FAB routes on h[:,0], which the media cannot reach when the anchor is after position 0. Experts therefore specialise only where h carries media. The FAB breadth cap is computed within modality (FAB_DOM_FRAC over the domains of the same top-level modality) so text's cap does not dilute. That is a small fabric change landing with Proposal 02's modality top level.
4. MEM stays text-only, with byte offsets that remain true. Captions are text and write normally. The per-source floor counts only domains that write, so pure-media domains do not dilute text floors.

DOM AND SIG
- Caption-byte signatures cannot separate two melody grammars: the captions look alike.
- So Proposal 01's M2 measurement comes first (stage 6).
- The planned answer is a two-level key: the modality from MediaSegment.modality (hard, exact), then within the modality a signature from AUD (pooled WORLD z, trained contrastively like SIG, sig_d 64). It feeds a per-modality DOM partition through the existing observe(signature, sample_window, tokens, now). The sample is the latent window, which ends before the anchor, so causality holds.
- The DOM spawn and merge thresholds are re-measured on latent signatures.

REPLAY ARMS
- Rehearsal from the synthetic holdout.
- Generative self-replay: the model can generate old areas' audio from their captions.
- OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM on each modality boundary.

MEASURING FORGETTING (exact, because the data is synthetic and labelled)
The R matrix per area, at every phase boundary, on both holdouts (in-distribution and compositional):
- caption bits/byte given media (understanding, in the existing unit);
- probe attribute accuracy of text-to-audio generations;
- grammar legality of continuations;
- codec recon L1;
- the text areas' bits/byte (the goal-B guard that media does not cost text).
Report ACC, BWT and FWT. Upper-bound arm: a joint i.i.d. run. Lower-bound arm: fine-tune only. Grounding is measured directly (attribute accuracy both ways), not only as loss, to catch hidden forgetting.
designs.generation:
WHAT GENERATES WHAT
- Text to audio: the caption is read by the LM. cond is the hidden state at the caption's last byte. WORLD.rollout(cond=h, steps=64, source='aud') produces WORLD latents z; AUD.from_world gives codec latents; AUD.decode gives log-mel; the vocoder stage (GPU, later) gives the waveform.
- Audio continuation: AUD.encode(prompt), then to_obs, then the WORLD encoder, then rollout from the prompt's context.
- Audio to text (understanding): the insert path with the ordinary text sampler.
- Video later uses the same rollout and a VID decoder.

TRAINING THE GENERATOR
- Teacher forcing alone does NOT work. Measured: notes 2-4 at chance (0.09-0.14) for both the WORLD arm and the no-WORLD arm, with or without 0.2 input noise.
- The free-running loss is required: roll out gen_len frames with gradients and take MSE against the true codec latents in AUD space. With it:
  - held-out text to audio: 100% all-four-notes-plus-timbre, L1 0.272;
  - audio continuation: grammar-legal note 3 in 0.988 of clips and note 4 in 0.973, timbre kept 1.0.
- It is deterministic: one output per prompt. Diversity needs a sampler, which is unsolved here. A GMM head over the next-latent delta was worse (legal 0.54-0.64), both with the target attached and detached. Planned arms: a GMM or diffusion head trained with free-running (Diffusion Forcing / MAR-style small MLP denoiser), or a hybrid discrete choice token.

EVALUATION (EVAL.generate_media)
- A from-scratch parameter-recovery probe is trained at build on TRUE generator output. In the prototype it was 100% on true and on reconstructed mels, so it measures the generator and not the probe.
- It is applied to generated media:
  - per-position note accuracy, timbre accuracy, and the all-attributes-correct rate;
  - grammar legality (continuations), measured against the known Markov table;
  - L1 against the decoded ground truth;
  - rollout divergence (the world.rollout.diverged counter, triggered when latent RMS exceeds WORLD_ROLLOUT_BOUND).
- Both holdouts are reported. On the compositional one this route currently generates the wrong first note in every clip (0.0), while notes 2-4 are 0.95-1.0 and timbre 1.0: memorisation of the caption-to-first-frame map at this scale.
- The text sampler (EVAL.generate) lands first; generate_media reuses its prompt and rng plumbing.
designs.world_model_role:
WORLD BECOMES THE MEDIA GENERATOR, NOT A SIDE HEAD
It holds the shared latent state for every observed stream, one encoder per source. It predicts that state forward with per-source predictor pools read through a causal context model. Its rollout, conditioned on the LM's hidden state, is the only path from text to audio or video. Its latents are also what the LM reads for understanding.

THIS INCLUDES WORLD IN MULTIMODAL TRAINING LITERALLY
Its loss_terms run on every media-bearing flush. Its rollout carries the generation loss. Its latent state carries the understanding signal.

MEASURED
- The REAL current WORLD (per-position MLP plus linear residual population, memoryless):
  - one-step MSE 0.56x persistence;
  - continuation note-3 legality 0.542, near the order-1 optimum of 0.469; note 4 at 0.228, chance;
  - text-conditioned rollout diverges (L1 6.8 / 84).
- WORLD_CTX='gru':
  - one-step 0.19x persistence; note 3 legal 0.887 but note 4 only 0.343 without the free-running loss;
  - 0.988 / 0.973 with it.
- The LM reading WORLD's z beat reading raw codec latents: 0.374 against 0.862 bits per caption, 0.94 against 0.82 exact.
- So the WORLD latent space earns its place. Generation through WORLD also beat a direct decoder without WORLD (1.0 against 0.875 all-correct).
- Single seed. Part of the gain may be parameter count: WORLD adds an encoder and readout.

DOES THE WORLD_FEEDBACK=within-noise GPU RESULT TRANSFER?
For text, no new information. There the forecast is a function of tokens the LM already reads, so it is a feature the LM learns itself (Q-WORLD-10).
For media in this route the LM has no other access to the clip, so conditioning on WORLD's state is not redundant: 9.7 to 0.37 bits per caption.
But what won is conditioning on the STATE, through the trunk. The FORECAST added post-trunk (the WORLD_FEEDBACK mechanism) was not measured to help, and its pooled post-trunk form was the weakest arm.
Prediction: forecast feedback stays near noise unless the text is ABOUT the clip's future.

PROPOSED GPU TEST
A synthetic task whose captions describe notes 3-4 given only notes 1-2 of audio, which only a forecast can answer. Five seeds, paired, as in gpu_world.sh.

UNCHANGED FOR TEXT
WORLD_FEEDBACK stays False for text and its wiring is untouched. WORLD_CTX='none' keeps text bit-identical.

REPORTING RULE
One-step inv against persistence must never be read as generation quality. W1 had the best one-step score (0.19) and poor rollouts; W1F scored 0.83 and had near-perfect rollouts. WORLD's counters gain rollout legality and divergence readings, each carrying its horizon and rollout length.

designs.costs:
COMPUTE PER MEDIA-BEARING WINDOW (CPU, one thread)
The real text window costs about 275 ms (3.64 win/s, map agent). Audio adds:
- codec training 3.8 ms, only during the codec phase (0 after the freeze, or when pre-encoded offline);
- context WORLD loss 9.8 ms;
- LM insert +1.0 ms;
- free-run generation loss 35 ms.
Total about 50 ms, or about +18%, when every window carries a clip and gen_every=1. With DATA_MEDIA_EVERY spacing so that 1 in 4 windows carries a clip, plus AUD_GEN_EVERY=2, it is about +3-5%.

GPU
- The free-running rollout is 64 sequential tiny GRU steps, so it is latency-bound (kernel launches), not FLOP-bound. With 12 runs sharing the card it will cost more than its FLOPs suggest.
- Mitigations: a shorter gen_len (32), cadence, or batching rollouts across the flush. The throughput agent should profile this before the 20k-window sweep.
- Text sequence length grows only 1.06x (K=8), which respects the stated throughput constraint.
- Training cost of the generator piece: 253 s against 98 s without free-run, i.e. 2.6x.

MEMORY
- Clip payloads: 64x128 log-mel floats, 32 KB per clip, or 2 KB per clip as frozen latents.
- A pre-encoded synthetic corpus of 100k clips is about 200 MB of latents.

ENGINEERING
- 2 new packages (26 entry points at video), 4 signature moves, about 17 audio-stage entry points, about 30 levers with census rows, and 4 owner rulings (CKPT absent field, OPT new group, media causality, M1).
- Zero new wires.
- TOK, MEM, SIG, CAP and RUN are unchanged. This is smaller than the discrete route on the text-path surgery (TOK reserved ranges, dead-row masks, CAP counting) and larger on WORLD and LM input.

OWNER GPU TIME
- Codec phase: about 100k+ steps for waveform fidelity with the vocoder (research-codecs estimate).
- WORLD and generator: minutes on GPU at this scale.
- Forgetting sweeps: 5 seeds x arms.
designs.risks:
Ranked by severity. Figures are measured unless marked.

1. EXPOSURE BIAS / ROLLOUT DRIFT. Continuous autoregressive generation trained only with teacher forcing collapses after the first note in every arm; input noise did not fix it. The free-running loss fixes it at 2.6x the generator's training cost and 35 ms per window on CPU. Any config with AUD_GEN_W=0 must be reported as not generating. startup_refusals should warn, and world.rollout.diverged plus the legality readings make it visible.

2. NO STOCHASTIC SAMPLER. The deterministic arm gives one continuation per prompt. Both GMM heads were worse (legal 0.54-0.64). A generator that cannot sample the 0.3 branch of the grammar is a mode-seeker. This is the biggest open quality gap of the continuous route; diffusion-head and hybrid-discrete arms are planned.

3. NO EXACT MEDIA LIKELIHOOD. There are no bits-per-frame for audio: M3 is answered only through caption bits/byte (understanding) and probe accuracy (generation). The R matrix mixes units, so every Reading must carry its unit.

4. COMPOSITIONAL GENERALISATION IS POOR at this scale.
   - Understanding on unseen combinations: 0.21-0.40 note accuracy.
   - Text to audio on unseen combinations: first note 0.0.
   - Scale or data variety may fix it; unmeasured.

5. WORLD's one-step inv reading is anti-correlated with generation quality. Selecting WORLD arms or growth on inv would pick the wrong arm. Rollout readings are mandatory.

6. CODEC DRIFT. Continuous latents have no discrete ids to pin their meaning. If the codec keeps training, WORLD, readout and LM inserts all see shifting inputs. Freezing per version is the design; the 'joint' arm is unmeasured.

7. WAVEFORM FIDELITY. The prototype stops at log-mel. The waveform vocoder is GPU-bound (phase not learned in CPU budgets per research-codecs). The owner decides whether a perceptual metric may use pretrained models; the design does not need one.

8. SIGNATURE / DOM. Caption text cannot separate media areas, so without the AUD signature (M2), DOM will lump every audio area into the caption-text domain and goal-B accounting is wrong. Unmeasured.

9. CONTRACT AND RESUME. Adding a modality to a text checkpoint is blocked by three guards until the NEW_PACKAGE / new-OPT-group rulings exist.

10. WORLD.lat=32 is fine for audio (readout MSE 0.0036-0.009 against latent variance 0.45) but probably too small for video. It is EXACT geometry, so raising it is a new-run decision.

11. GPU LATENCY of sequential rollouts under 12-way sharing (unmeasured).

12. EVIDENCE QUALITY. Single seed, 1.5-2k steps, and a stand-in LM that mirrors the gru arm (not the real LM package) for stages 3-4. The WORLD-against-no-WORLD generation gap (1.0 against 0.875) may be partly parameter count.

13. CAUSALITY. The insert must follow its anchor. If a mis-mapped anchor puts the clip at the window start ahead of preceding text, those tokens peek at later stream content (Q-FAB-7). test_causality must cover this.
designs.rejected_alternatives:
MEASURED AND REJECTED AS DEFAULTS (all kept as arms; nothing is removed)
- Memoryless WORLD (today's per-position MLP plus linear residual population) as the media dynamics model: continuation note 4 at chance (0.228), text-conditioned rollout diverges (L1 6.8 / 84). Default for media is WORLD_CTX='gru'; 'none' stays the text default.
- Teacher forcing only (with or without 0.2 input noise): notes 2-4 at chance. Replaced by the free-running loss.
- LM.encode(extra=) pooled post-trunk, today's hook, as the media input: 0.485 note accuracy.
- extra_attn (learned position queries, fits the current signature): 0.80, below insert's 0.978. It remains the fallback if the owner refuses the LM.encode move.
- Full-rate insert (K=64): worse (0.882) and +43% LM step time against +5.8% for K=8.
- GMM stochastic head as the default: worse than deterministic (legal 0.54-0.64 against 0.99), with the target attached or detached. Retried later with a free-running loss, or as a diffusion head.
- Direct text-to-latent generator bypassing WORLD (T0): worse (0.875 against 1.0 all-correct, L1 0.645 against 0.272), and it drops the owner's world-model-included requirement.

REJECTED ON STRUCTURE OR EVIDENCE
- Media bytes or codec ids in Stream.bytes / TOK: the bpt shift and BPE-eats-codes risks the map measured. This route never puts media in the byte stream.
- Split clock kinds per modality: every cadence lever would multiply. Media rides its anchored text window, so one Windows kind suffices, with Frames for in-clip lengths.
- Back-propagating LM, WORLD or generation losses into the codec encoder: REPA-E latent collapse and STE instability in the literature; codec drift is also a goal-B hazard.
- Separate World instances per modality: no shared latent, so no cross-modal (AV) prediction, and the WORLD pieces would be duplicated. Rejected for one World with per-source encoders and pools.
- Feeding WORLD the LM hidden state instead of observation embeddings: lm/api.py:510-514 already refuses this, and it would break the new-sense plug.
- A new cross-package wire for LM.width or WORLD.lat into AUD: the root-argument idiom costs no wire budget.

designs.route:
HYBRID. Two paths share one learned codec.

Discrete path, for understanding and generation by the LM: a from-scratch FSQ audio codec (a single codebook, 1000 codes, 50 frames/s, one token per frame) emits codes into the ONE shared stream. The codes sit in per-modality embedding and head tables that LM owns. They are carried as transport-encoded ids in the ordinary (B,L) id tensor, and a typed-segment output mask confines each position's softmax to its own modality.

Continuous path, for prediction and cross-modal forecasting: the same codec's pre-quantisation latents (64-d, 50 Hz) feed a new TEMPORAL media head in WORLD. The head predicts the frozen codec latent 1 and 5 frames ahead, conditioned on the text context. Its forecast can feed back into LM.encode through the existing extra= path (WORLD_FEEDBACK, ships False).

Modality is a first-class segment type for everything else:
- DATA: typed segments.
- SIG: a 'typed' unit space.
- DOM: media domains.
- FAB: learned routing by default, with modality expert groups as an arm.
- MEM: stays text-only.
- EVAL: new metrics per modality unit, plus exact grounding scores taken from the synthetic generator's own parameters.

Video (VID) later follows the same shape.
designs.summary:
Why the hybrid, from the literature:
- Every from-scratch any-to-any system that also generates (Chameleon, Unified-IO 2, Emu3, VideoPoet) generated discrete codes from ONE trunk, and discrete codes keep an exact likelihood (M3).
- Gemini and Janus show continuous features are the better input for understanding.
- The WORLD model is the natural home for continuous cross-modal prediction (V-JEPA, Genie).
So the codes carry generation and LM understanding, and WORLD carries continuous prediction, over the same frozen codec.

What I measured on CPU, synthetic audio, a few minutes per run (files are in the scratch dir design-hybrid/):

(1) Codec.
- A spectral FSQ codec learned from scratch trains in 250 s on one CPU thread: 5,614 steps, 724k params.
- Held-out log-mel distance is 0.463. For scale: silence scores 1.706, and Griffin-Lim on the TRUE magnitude spectrum scores 0.185.
- Held-out use: 630 of 1000 codes, 7.46 bits per code.
- Encoding runs 1250x faster than real time.
- The analytic parameter-recovery probe scores 100% on ground-truth audio and 40% exact on codec reconstructions (band 0.98, kind 0.77, timbre 0.60, count 0.72). That 40% is the ceiling for any generation.
- The waveform SEANet codec the codec research used produced near-silent output on this data after 2,153 steps: RMS 0.002-0.02 against 0.15-0.46 input, and probe accuracy at chance. It moves to a GPU arm.

(2) LM on the codes. A width-128 GRU with the modality mask, trained on 24k fresh clips for 6,000 steps:
- 2.45 bits per code on held-out audio.
- Understanding (audio to caption): 54% exact attributes (band 0.98, timbre 0.93, kind 0.81, count 0.73).
- Generation (caption to audio, temperature 0.7): 16.7% exact, i.e. 42% of the codec's ceiling.
- Held-out attribute combinations: 0% exact for understanding and 8% for generation, so there is no composition yet.
- With a fixed 2,400-clip set the model overfits (held-out bits per code 3.44 at 3,000 steps, 4.51 at 9,000). Width 256 lifts generation to 21% and understanding to 46% on the small set.

(3) Forgetting and the mask.
- Adding audio after text with no replay raises text bits/byte from 1.94 to 7.85.
- 25% text replay removes it: 1.936 before, 1.931 after, with audio no worse (3.26 against 3.44 bits per code).
- The mask saves 0.06 bits/byte during the text-only phase and removes the 5.9% of sampled audio tokens that the joint softmax spends on non-code ids.
- In the real tree, widening vocab_slots from 4096 to 5120 costs 11-13% windows/s (4.7 to 4.1-4.2 w/s). That is why codes get their own tables rather than sitting in the BPE id space.

(4) WORLD on codec latents. Error relative to the persistence baseline at 5 frames ahead:
- today's memoryless residual-linear predictor: 0.678
- a temporal GRU: 0.386
- a caption-conditioned GRU: 0.314

But WORLD cannot be the generator. Its open-loop deterministic rollouts collapse: mel 1.12-1.70 (caption-only 1.70, about silence) and 3-12% exact.

Decisions this design asks the owner to rule on:
- M1: one Windows clock.
- M4: one package per modality.
- M5: per-modality tables with transport ids.
- M8: WORLD owns continuous cross-modal prediction.
- M10: yes, adding a modality is adding an area.

Change count: 12 new entry points (137 -> 149), 2 signature moves (LM.decode, DATA.data_plan), 2 new cross-package wires (19 -> 21 of 25), and one CKPT/OPT ruling for fields absent from old checkpoints.
designs.architecture:
DATA FLOW PER EPOCH AND PER FLUSH (media off leaves every text path bit-identical)

1. DATA.draw_stream returns a Stream whose `bytes` field is the concatenation of the TEXT segments only, so every byte consumer keeps working unchanged. A new field `segments` holds an ordered list of typed records:
   - Seg(kind='text' | 'aud', area, byte_anchor, payload, params, pair_id, task)
   - payload is bytes for text, a waveform tensor for audio.
   - params is the generator's parameter tuple, used for grounding.
   - task is one of 'a' (plain audio), 't2a' or 'a2t'.
   Synthetic media clips are drawn FRESH every epoch from per-epoch child streams. I measured that a fixed clip set overfits: held-out bits per code went 3.44 -> 4.51 between 3k and 9k steps, against 2.45 with 10x fresh clips.

2. The TOK segmentation is unchanged and is applied to text segments only. bytes_per_token is therefore measured on text by construction, which neutralises map risk 1: the SIG width can no longer shrink silently.

3. At the epoch roll, AUD.encode runs over every media segment once the codec is frozen: 24,144 s of audio encoded in 15.8 s on one thread. It returns codes (F frames) and latents (F x AUD_D). The root builds ONE id sequence by interleaving:
   - text ids;
   - media markers and codes, as transport ids from spine.derive.media_id(modality, code) = MEDIA_BASE + modality*2^20 + code, with MEDIA_BASE = 2^24, far above any vocab_slots.
   A parallel int8 `modality` array and a `frame_pos` array are added to Segmentation as record fields; this is not a signature change. For media positions byte_pos holds the segment's byte anchor, and MEM never receives those positions.

4. Per window (A stage):
   - SIG under SIG_SPACE='typed' signs the last width units ending before the window. A unit is a byte for text and a code for audio, so the Q-FAB-7 causality rule holds.
   - DOM.observe receives tokens filtered to text ids, so tokc histograms stay text-only.
   - TOK.on_window skips any pair involving an id outside its table. This is a generic guard with no signature move.

5. Per flush (B stage):
   - obs_emb = LM.embed(x) with the signature unchanged: LM routes ids >= MEDIA_BASE to its media table. world/api.py's claim that "a second sense needs new rows in LM's embedding and nothing new here" is thereby honoured literally, and WORLD.loss_terms runs unchanged over mixed windows.
   - New row: WORLD.media_terms(latents, valid, context=h at the segment's BEGIN marker) adds the temporal media prediction loss.
   - LM.encode is unchanged; extra = forecast plus media_forecast, and both are None at the default WORLD_FEEDBACK=False.
   - LM.decode(..., modality=) builds the logits. A text-only window computes the text head only, so its cost and bits are identical to today. A window containing media computes a virtual concatenation [text rows | aud rows]. Positions predicting a text token are masked to text rows plus each enabled modality's BEGIN row; positions predicting a code are masked to that modality's codes plus its END row. Under the mask, this is mathematically what separate heads compute.
   - lm_loss maps transport ids to columns internally.
   - FAB receives a head closure that the root rebinds per flush with the modality array, and targets already mapped to columns, so FAB stays id-agnostic.
   - MEM.write and MEM.read apply to text positions only.

6. Loss:
   - total += text CE (per text unit) + AUD_LM_W x code CE (per code unit) + WORLD_MEDIA_W x media_terms.
   - During the codec phase it also adds AUD.loss_terms on a media waveform batch.
   - Every term reports in its own unit (bits/byte, bits/code, bits/s = 50 x bits/code) and the units are never summed in one reading.

7. Codec phase (the owner's "learned inside the framework"):
   - While windows < AUD_FREEZE_AT, AUD trains on media areas under its own OPT group 'codec', in parallel with ordinary text LM training. The LM never sees audio while the codes are still moving.
   - At the freeze, the codec's weights are hashed into aud.version, the codec is frozen, and media areas become eligible for the LM phases of DATA_PHASE_SCHED.
   - A startup refusal fires if the first media LM phase begins before AUD_FREEZE_AT.
   - Nothing back-propagates from the LM into the codec (the REPA-E, STE-collapse and AQM evidence).

8. Generation: EVAL.generate becomes a sampler. Given a prompt such as [T2A-marker] caption [AUD_BEGIN], it samples a declared number of frames under the audio mask. END is masked until the requested duration: the prototype emitted a premature END 0.7-4% of the time without this. AUD.decode then produces the waveform, and DATA.recover_params gives the exact attribute score.

ONE CLOCK (M1). The Windows kind stays single. A window is LM_CTX positions of the unified stream in any modality, and every cadence stays in Windows. Named conversions go in spine/derive.py:
- frames_per_second(sr, hop)
- media_seconds_per_window(ctx, fps)
- media_id and media_code (the transport encoding)
Each gets a known-answer table in tests/test_derive.py. spine/units.py gains unit LABELS only (FRAMES='frames', HZ='Hz'), not clock kinds.

Single-codebook FSQ is chosen so that one position is one frame. WORLD horizons within a media segment are then frames with no conversion, and flattened RVQ's 4x sequence cost never arises.
designs.codecs:
AUD (built now) and VID (later, same shape): one package per modality (M4), PREFIX AUD / VID.

AUD CODEC, DEFAULT ARM 'spec' (measured):
- Features: STFT log-magnitude, n_fft 512, hop 160 at 8 kHz, i.e. 50 frames/s.
- Encoder: Conv1d(257->256, k3) ELU, Conv1d(256->256, k3) ELU, Conv1d(256->64, k1). This 64-d latent is the WORLD observation.
- Quantiser: GroupNorm, then FSQ levels 8,5,5,5 (1000 codes, 9.97 bits nominal), plus the per-dimension marginal-entropy bonus at weight 1.0 (AUD_ENT_W). The codec research found plain FSQ collapsed in 3 of 5 runs and this bonus fixed it.
- Decoder: a mirror conv stack predicting log-magnitude.
- Waveform: Griffin-Lim, 32 iterations. It is a fixed algorithm with no learned or pretrained weights, so the from-scratch rule holds.
- Loss: L1 on log-magnitude + 2 x L1 on magnitude + entropy bonus.
- Measured: 724k params; 250 s of CPU for 5,614 steps at batch 16 x 0.5 s. Held-out mel 0.463 (silence 1.706; oracle Griffin-Lim on the true magnitude 0.185). 630 of 1000 codes used, entropy 7.46 bits/code (373 bit/s), output RMS 0.16 against 0.27 input. Encode RTF 0.0008; decode RTF 0.031 with Griffin-Lim 32.
- Probe accuracy on reconstructions: 40% exact (band 0.98, kind 0.77, timbre 0.60, count 0.72). Timbre is the weak attribute: harmonic structure gets blurred.

AUD ARM 'wave' (GPU only):
- SEANet 1-D conv encoder/decoder, the research codec's architecture, with the same FSQ plus entropy bonus. GAN and feature-matching losses and quantiser dropout are added on the owner's GPU (DAC/EnCodec-scale step counts, 100k-400k).
- Measured on my data: 2,153 steps / 486 s CPU gave mel 1.169, output RMS 0.002-0.02 (near-silent) and probe exact 0.028, i.e. chance.
- This also suggests the research table's "SNR ~0 dB" rows reflect a near-silent decoder, not only lost phase. It is worth re-checking before any number from those rows becomes a default.

AUD LEVERS (all with census amendment rows):

| Lever | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| AUD_ENABLED | False | Null codec. D4 pattern: every entry point answers inertly; text stays bit-identical. |
| AUD_ARCH | 'spec' | choices spec \| wave |
| AUD_SR | 8000 | Hz |
| AUD_HOP | 160 | samples; gives 50 frames/s |
| AUD_LEVELS | '8,5,5,5' | |
| AUD_D | 64 | latent width |
| AUD_HID | 256 | |
| AUD_ENT_W | 1.0 | |
| AUD_LR | 1e-3 | |
| AUD_FREEZE_AT | Windows(20000) | 0 = never train; load only |
| AUD_GL_ITERS | 32 | |
| AUD_COLLAPSE_MIN | 64 | codes used per batch below this fires aud.collapse |
| AUD_LM_W | 1.0 | weight of code-position CE, per code unit. Emu3.5 used 0.5 on vision tokens; this is the knob for that. |

AUD entry points (8):
- build(aud, *, device, rng) -> Codec, a null Codec when disabled
- encode(aud, codec, wave) -> CodecOut(codes, latents)
- decode(aud, codec, codes) -> wave
- loss_terms(aud, codec, wave) -> CodecStep(loss, codes_used, entropy_bits)
- geometry(aud, codec)
- state_dict(aud, codec)
- load_into(aud, codec, sd)
- counters(aud, codec)
Codec.parameters() exists and is listed in compose._base_parameters' sibling for the 'codec' group, so it cannot silently train nothing (map risk 12).

Counters (did it fire):
- aud.built ('live' | 'null')
- aud.loss_terms.calls
- aud.codes_used and aud.entropy_bits (gauges)
- aud.collapse: PRESENT-AND-0 while armed, fires below AUD_COLLAPSE_MIN. Collapse is silent in the loss curve (7 of 15 research runs collapsed).
- aud.frozen (0 until the freeze, then 1)
- aud.encode.calls
- aud.version

VID (stage 7):

designs.synthetic_data:
GENERATOR (prototype: design-hybrid/synth.py, becomes DATA's synthetic media family)
Every clip is rendered from an explicit parameter tuple, and the paired caption is rendered from the same tuple by a template. Understanding and generation are therefore scored EXACTLY by an analytic parameter-recovery probe: STFT energy runs, harmonic-sum pitch, log-pitch slope and harmonic energy fraction. The probe uses fixed signal processing with no learned model.

The prototype family, "aud/beeps-and-tones":
- kind: tone, rise, fall or beeps
- band: low 180-260 Hz, mid 450-650 Hz, high 1100-1500 Hz
- timbre: pure or buzzy (7 harmonics at 1/k)
- count: 2-4 for beeps
- jitter: amplitude, onset and frequency, plus optional noise
That gives 36 combinations, 1 s clips at 8 kHz, i.e. 50 codes. Captions look like "three low pure beeps" or "a high buzzy rising chirp".

Probe validation: 360 of 360 correct on ground truth after one fix (the pitch search range originally stopped at 1.7 kHz and missed high chirps).

Held-out:
- a seed-disjoint block per area, from the existing data.holdout.<key> child (fixes map risk 11: synthetic currently holds nothing out);
- HELD-OUT COMBINATIONS that never appear in training, for a composition test: rise/high/buzzy, fall/mid/pure, 3-low-pure beeps, 2-high-buzzy beeps.

DATA levers:

| Lever | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| DATA_MEDIA | "" | media area names under the slash rule, e.g. 'aud/tones,aud/beeps,aud/syllables' |
| DATA_MEDIA_SECONDS | 600 | media seconds per epoch |
| DATA_MEDIA_CLIP_S | 1.0 | |
| DATA_MEDIA_TASKS | 't2a,a2t,a' | task mixture; VideoPoet-style prefixes |
| DATA_MEDIA_HOLDOUT | 0.1 | |
| DATA_MEDIA_HOLD_COMBOS | 'auto' | 4 per area, drawn from data.holdout.<key> |
| DATA_TEXT_SHARE | 0.25 | text rehearsal share inside media phases; measured sufficient below |

Real data later lands in the SAME slots: a real audio area is an 'aud/<name>' area whose segments carry waveforms, with no params, so it gets no grounding score (bits per code only).

Area families after the prototype, in build order:
1. aud/beeps-and-tones (measured).
2. aud/chirps-am-fm.
3. aud/syllables: Klatt-style vowels and consonant bursts, reusing codec_lib's syllables().
4. aud/melodies: 8-note scale; the caption lists the notes.
5. Paired audio-video later: vid/bounce 2-D, where a collision emits a click and shape maps to pitch. This gives WORLD a physics forecasting target and cross-modal grounding in both directions.

Text for the forgetting benchmark uses the existing synthetic order-2 Markov areas. The one in my prototype has a floor of 1.826 bits/byte.

Cost: the generator takes about 0.4 ms per clip, and the frozen codec encodes about 1,250 s of audio per second on one thread. Regenerating every epoch is therefore cheap, and it is mandatory: measured overfitting on a fixed set.

designs.continual_learning:
MODALITY = AREA (M10: yes). Every synthetic media family is a DATA area under the slash rule ('aud/tones', 'aud/syllables', later 'vid/bounce'). DATA_PHASE_SCHED already accepts area names, and Plan.protocol already recognises rehearsed against pure-add (Q-DATA-7). A modality-incremental benchmark is therefore a schedule, for example 'eng|eng|aud/tones|aud/syllables|eng'. The codec phase runs during the text phases and must be frozen before the first media phase (startup refusal).

PROTECTION, measured at toy scale (width-128 GRU; P1 = 1500 text steps, then P2 = 3000 audio steps):

| Arm | Text bits/byte before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| joint softmax, no replay | 1.997 | 8.549 | +6.55 |
| mask, no replay | 1.936 | 7.846 | +5.91 |
| mask + 25% text replay | 1.936 | 1.931 | -0.005 |

With replay, audio also did slightly better: 3.26 against 3.44 bits per code, and understanding was the same, 32% exact.

Defaults this implies:
- A media phase is REHEARSED, with DATA_TEXT_SHARE=0.25. DeepSeek-VL used 30%; my run shows 25% suffices at this scale.
- The pure-add protocol stays as the measured lower-bound arm.
- The typed mask is ALSO protection. Under it, code positions never push text head rows down (the joint arm forgot 0.64 bits/byte more), and during text-only phases the untrained media rows are out of the softmax denominator (0.06 bits/byte cheaper).

Further isolation arms, measured on GPU by the owner:
- FAB_MOD_GROUPS: hard modality expert blocks, MoMa-style, against learned routing (Shukor). Breadth cap, grow and cull act inside a block, so media domains cannot change text's FAB_DOM_FRAC denominator.
- Upcycling new-modality experts from text experts (MoE-LLaVA), the analogue of LM_NEW_ROW_INIT='mean'.
- OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM re-warm at the modality boundary (Ibrahim 2024).
- Generative self-replay from the model's own old-modality samples: possible because it generates every modality.

DOM, FAB and MEM:
- DOM spawns media domains through the typed signature. The M2 measurement in stage 4 checks whether the leading signature dimensions go to modality, as Proposal 01 predicts. If they do, Proposal 02's modality-top/content-leaf split becomes the next step.
- DOM tokc stays text-only.
- MEM stays text-only in this route. Its per-source floor counts text domains only, so adding media never shrinks text's protected memory. Media retrieval (keys from codec latents) is a later arm.

MEASURING FORGETTING WITH SYNTHETIC LABELS. The R matrix R[phase_end][area] is filled at every phase boundary from the fixed seed-disjoint holdout. Each cell carries:
(a) bits per unit in the area's own unit (bits/byte for text, bits/code and bits/s for audio);
(b) GROUNDING, from EVAL.grounding: understanding exact attribute accuracy (audio -> caption) and generation exact attribute accuracy (caption -> audio -> recover_params), each split into train combinations and held-out combinations.
Grounding catches "hidden forgetting" (Chen 2026), where the loss survives but grounding moves. ACC, BWT and FWT use the existing forgetting_of and bwt_of per metric. Units are never mixed. DOM.note_competence receives bits per unit normalised by the modality's running baseline, so competence comparisons stay within one modality (M3).

CODEC DRIFT is handled by freezing plus versioning (see codecs). A codec version change is recorded as a new alphabet, the same as adding an area. It is never a silent change of meaning under old rows.
designs.generation:
HOW IT WORKS
Generation is next-token sampling of discrete codes by the SAME routed LM path used for reading. There is no second forward (M7), so ISSUES P1-C4/C5-style drift between two paths cannot arise.

EVAL.generate becomes the sampler. Proposal 01's "text sampler first" is stage 2, and the audio sampler is the same function with a modality argument:
- The prompt comes from prompts_by_domain; for media areas that is DATA's held-out captions with a task marker and AUD_BEGIN.
- Each step calls logits_fn(ids, modality), i.e. LM.decode under the typed mask. Audio positions choose among codes plus END, and END is masked until the requested frame count.
- Temperature is EVAL_GEN_TEMP.
- Then AUD.decode: FSQ unpack, conv decoder, Griffin-Lim; later a GAN-trained waveform decoder on the 'wave' arm.

Understanding uses the same machinery in the other direction: an audio prompt, greedy caption, parse.

EVALUATION is EXACT because the data is synthetic. DATA.recover_params (analytic) is applied to:
- the ground truth, which must read 100% or the reading is refused;
- codec reconstructions, which give the ceiling;
- generated clips, which give the score.
Scores are per attribute and exact, split into train and held-out combinations. They sit beside bits per code on the held-out set, the codec's own mel distance, and codes used / entropy of the generated codes (a mode-collapse check).

MEASURED (codec ceiling 40% exact, band 0.98):

| Arm | Held-out bits/code | Understanding exact | Generation exact | Generation band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W128, 2.4k clips, 3k steps (mask) | 3.44 | 32% | 7% (T=1) | 0.53 |
| W128, 24k fresh clips, 6k steps | 2.45 | 54% | 16.7% (T=0.7) | 0.72 |
| W256, 2.4k clips, 4.5k steps | 4.30 (overfit) | 46% | 20.8% (T=0.7) | — |

Notes on the table:
- Understanding in the 24k-clip row: band 0.98, timbre 0.93, kind 0.81, count 0.73.
- Held-out combinations: understanding 0% exact in every arm; generation 0-8%. There is no compositional generalisation at this scale.
- The joint-softmax arm sampled non-code ids in 5.9% of audio positions (T=1); the mask removes this by construction.

So generation works, but it is data-limited and then capacity-limited. On the 24k set it reaches about 42% of the codec ceiling. The limits are the codec's timbre fidelity and the LM's width and data. Both scale on the owner's GPU.

CONTINUOUS ARMS, for later and judged on grounding accuracy per FLOP:
- a GMM/diffusion head on WORLD's media latent (GIVT, MAR, Diffusion Forcing);
- a factorised FSQ head (8+5+5+5 = 23 logits instead of 1000).
designs.world_model_role:
WORLD stays enabled and is part of multimodal training in three ways:

(1) UNCHANGED TEXT PATH OVER MIXED WINDOWS. WORLD.loss_terms(obs_emb = LM.embed(x)) runs as today. On media windows, obs_emb contains the media rows' embeddings: the module's own "new rows in LM's embedding and nothing new here" design, honoured with no WORLD edit. With media off it is bit-identical.

(2) NEW TEMPORAL MEDIA HEAD, WORLD.media_terms. It predicts the frozen codec's continuous pre-quantisation latent (64-d, 50 Hz) at horizons of 1 and 5 frames (20 and 100 ms), with a causal GRU over the latent history. Optionally, h0 is conditioned on the text context: the LM hidden state at the segment's BEGIN, or the caption.

Measured on held-out, error relative to persistence (horizon 1 / horizon 5):

| Predictor | h1 | h5 | Params |
|---|---|---|---|
| today's memoryless residual-linear (z + zP) | 0.321 | 0.678 | 8k |
| memoryless MLP | 0.162 | 0.567 | |
| temporal GRU | 0.134 | 0.386 | 91k |
| caption-conditioned GRU | 0.138 | 0.314 | 140k |

So temporal context nearly halves the 100 ms error against WORLD's present form, and text conditioning takes another 19%. This is where cross-modal prediction lives (M8), and it is the V-JEPA / Genie-dynamics role.

Because the target is the FROZEN codec latent:
- no anti-collapse term is needed on this path (the historic WORLD_W folding defect cannot recur here);
- forecasts are DECODABLE: 1-step teacher-forced forecasts decode to mel 0.47-0.50 against the codec's own 0.46.

(3) FEEDBACK, ship-off. WORLD.media_forecast gives a born-zero world_proj_media(pred latent) added to LM.encode's extra at media positions. This is the Janus split: continuous features in, discrete codes out. It ships inert behind WORLD_FEEDBACK=False, per Q-WORLD-10. The GPU A/B on audio is the owner's experiment Q8: next-chunk structure in audio may be worth what text was not.

WHAT WORLD IS NOT, measured: a generator by deterministic rollout. Open-loop rollouts decoded through the codec collapse:
- from a 10-frame prompt: mel 1.12-1.16, 6-12% exact;
- from the caption alone: mel 1.70 (silence-level), 3% exact.
Generation therefore stays with the LM's discrete sampler. A stochastic WORLD media head (GMM or Diffusion Forcing) is a later arm, not a default.

COMPUTE PER MEDIA SECOND
- 50 positions, i.e. 0.39 windows at LM_CTX=128. A T2A or A2T pair (about 15 caption tokens + 52 media positions) fits in about half a window.
- Media windows skip TOK.on_window and MEM.write/read (text-only), so their fixed A-stage Python cost is at most the text window's.
- The LM cost per position is modality-independent (prototype: 5.4-8.7 ms per 96-position window at W128 on CPU).
- Text-only windows keep today's head width because media tables are separate. A joint table would have cost 11-13% on EVERY window in the tree measurement (4.7 -> 4.1-4.2 w/s).
- Mixed windows pay a head over vocab_slots + 1002 columns.

CODEC
- The spec codec trains in minutes on CPU (724k params). On GPU it is negligible.
- Encoding is offline at the epoch roll, at 1250x real time on one CPU thread. Regenerating a fresh synthetic epoch of 10 minutes of audio costs well under 1 s of encoding.
- Decode for eval only: Griffin-Lim 32 at 0.031 RTF.
- The wave arm is a GPU job at literature scale: DAC used 400k iterations; for this size that is unverified.

WORLD MEDIA HEAD
- About 91-140k params: a GRU of WORLD_HID=128 over 50 frames per media segment. Small next to the LM.

PARAMETERS
- LM media rows: 2 x 1002 x 128 ≈ 256k at LM_WIDTH=128.
- The codec's 724k sit in their own OPT group, stepped only in the codec phase.

GPU EXTRAPOLATION (unmeasured here)
- On GPU, sequence length rather than Python dominates. Media adds positions at 50/s, the same rate as the most compressed published codecs' 40-75 tokens/s, so the multiplier is bounded.
- The 38 -> 2-3 windows/s late slowdown is orthogonal. This route does not lengthen windows (LM_CTX stays 128); it adds windows in proportion to media seconds.

ENGINEERING

designs.risks:
Ranked by how silently each one would hurt:

1. GENERATION QUALITY at small scale is the weakest measured link. It reached 17-21% exact, against 40% for the codec ceiling and 100% for ground truth. With 2.4k clips, longer training made held-out bits per code WORSE (3.44 -> 4.51); only fresh data fixed it (2.45).
   Mitigations: regenerate synthetic media every epoch (a DATA rule, not an option); owner GPU width and data sweeps; the factorised FSQ-head and continuous-head arms.

2. NO COMPOSITIONAL GENERALISATION. 0% exact understanding on held-out attribute combinations in every arm. It shows only in the combination split, which is why EVAL.grounding reports that split separately and never just the pooled number.

3. TOTAL FORGETTING WITHOUT REHEARSAL. Text went to 7.8-8.5 bits/byte from 1.94. The rehearsed protocol with 25% text is the default for media phases, and a pure-add phase must print its protocol (Plan.protocol already does).

4. CODEC FIDELITY. The spec plus Griffin-Lim codec has timbre 0.60 and does not learn phase. The waveform codec failed on CPU (near-silent output). The research agent's SNR~0 dB rows likely hide the same near-silence.
   The aud.collapse counter covers code collapse, but NOT a quiet decoder. An aud.recon_rms_ratio gauge with a did-it-fire threshold is needed.

5. TRANSPORT-ID COUPLING. Ids >= 2^24 carry meaning. The mitigations:
   - the encoding lives in spine.derive with known-answer tests;
   - LM refuses unknown modality ranges;
   - TOK and DOM guard by table membership rather than by knowing the encoding.
   A package that indexes a vocab_slots-sized tensor with a raw id still breaks. A grep-style ownership test that lists vocab-indexed sites should be added.

6. WIRE BUDGET. 21 of 25 after AUD and 23 with VID. The next modality needs a ruling on multi-source wires.

7. SIG/DOM on the typed space (M2) is unmeasured. Domain thresholds were tuned on bytes, and modality may dominate the signature's leading dimensions.

8. CODEC DRIFT versus continual learning. Freeze plus versioning works, but a real-data retrain doubles the media rows per version.

9. TRANSFORMER ARM. Chameleon-style modality-competition norm growth. Mitigations: LM_QK_NORM and LM_Z_LOSS levers, logit-norm gauges per modality; OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 is a flagged risk for multimodal runs.

10. METRIC MIXING. Any report that averages bits/byte with bits/code is meaningless. Units are labelled on every reading, and competence is normalised within each modality.

11. SCALE GAP. Everything here is at 0.5-1.4M params on toy synthetic audio with one seed per configuration.

12. The CKPT absent-field ruling weakens the "refuse a missing field" guard. It is limited to fields declared with absent=, and every born tensor is listed.
designs.rejected_alternatives:
- CODES INSIDE THE BPE ID SPACE (one joint table under LM_VOCAB_SLOTS).
  Measured costs:
  - +0.06 bits/byte on text during text-only phases, from untrained code rows in the softmax;
  - 5.9% of sampled audio positions spent on non-code ids;
  - 0.64 bits/byte more forgetting than the masked arm;
  - 11-13% fewer windows/s in the real tree at 5120 vs 4096 slots, paid by EVERY text window.
  Structural costs: vocab_slots MAY_WIDEN moves a top-anchored block; CAP's and TOK's row counts would include codes; BPE's longest-match and minting would eat serialised codes (map risk 2).

- PURE CONTINUOUS THROUGH WORLD. Measured WORLD rollouts collapse (mel 1.12-1.70, 3-12% exact), so it cannot generate without a stochastic head. It also needs an LM input-path signature move, because extra= is post-trunk, and it loses the exact likelihood (M3).

- FLATTENED RVQ. 4x sequence length (200 tokens/s). Single-codebook FSQ at 50 Hz matched the continuous ceiling in the research runs.

- WAVEFORM SEANet CODEC AS THE CPU DEFAULT. Near-silent output at 2k steps. Kept as the GPU 'wave' arm.

- JOINT CODEC + LM TRAINING (back-propagating LM loss into the codec). REPA-E latent collapse, STE codebook collapse, and AQM's point that old codes must stay decodable. The codec trains in its own phase and is frozen.

- SPLIT CLOCK KINDS PER MODALITY (M1). Multiplies every cadence lever. A single-codebook frame-rate codec makes one position one frame, so one Windows kind suffices.

- HARD MODALITY EXPERT GROUPS AS THE DEFAULT. Shukor 2025 (learned routing wins) conflicts with MoMa. Kept as the FAB_MOD_GROUPS arm to measure.

- MEM OVER MEDIA IN THE FIRST CUT. It needs a modality coordinate, and media sources would dilute text's floor. Deferred to an arm keyed on codec latents.

- A SECOND GENERATION FORWARD. It would repeat the ISSUES P1-C4/C5 two-path divergence; the sampler reuses the reading path.

- PRETRAINED ENCODERS / PERCEPTUAL METRICS. Excluded by the from-scratch rule. The analytic probe replaces learned metrics for synthetic data.

judge.rationale:
1. WHY DISCRETE-IN-THE-STREAM BEATS CONTINUOUS-THROUGH-WORLD AS THE BACKBONE
- Two of the three designers measured independently that WORLD cannot be the generator by deterministic rollout:
  - Route 2 T0W: log-mel L1 6.8/84, diverged.
  - Route 3: rollouts reach mel 1.12-1.70 and 3-12% exact.
- Route 2 fixed rollout only with a new context GRU, a free-running loss that costs 2.6x training and 35 ms per window, and a deterministic generator with no sampler. Its GMM heads measured worse (0.54-0.64 against 0.99 legal).
- Its headline "100% text-to-audio" comes from a task where the caption spells out all four notes, so a deterministic regressor is optimal. On unseen combinations the first note was wrong in every clip (0.0).
- It also gives up exact media likelihood (M3), which the whole goal-B R matrix is built on.
- The discrete path generates by the same next-token sampler as text: one forward path, the ISSUES P1-C4/C5 lesson. It has exact bits per code, and every surveyed from-scratch any-to-any generator (Chameleon, Unified-IO 2, Emu3, VideoPoet) used it.

2. WHY ROUTE 1 OVER ROUTE 3
They agree on almost everything that matters. Route 1 is ahead on:
- Evidence quality: it ran compose() -> sysm.model and sysm.world, the tree's own GRU and WORLD with tree-TOK ids. It measured WORLD's forgetting (3x on pure-add, contained by replay), and it measured that 25 Hz codes are easier for the LM at every budget.
- Goal B: DOM and FAB act per modality class, and WORLD's cross-modality pairs are masked.
Route 3 is ahead on three points, and the merged design takes all three:
- Contract economy: filter at the root instead of moving DOM.observe or MEM signatures.
- A real WORLD role over continuous latents: temporal GRU 0.386 against memoryless 0.678, relative to persistence at 100 ms.
- A codec that uses its codebook: 559-630 codes against Route 1's 109 at 25 Hz.
Route 3 also found that its SEANet waveform codec produced near-silent output at CPU budget. That is a real warning about the "SNR about 0 dB" rows, and it becomes the aud.quiet gauge.

3. WHAT I CHECKED
- The prototype JSONs match the numbers claimed: Cpure/Creplay; Jout25L; stage4_T1_f1 (combo first note 0.0); lm_mask_replay 1.936 -> 1.931; lm_mask_big 2.45 bits/code and 53.9% exact.
- In the tree:
  - the dead-row suffix mask at lm/api.py decode, dead[int(live_vocab):]=True;
  - ckpt/api.py's missing-field refusal;
  - WIRE_BUDGET=25 with 19 spent;
  - the §7 count of 137;
  - EVAL.generate and WORLD.manage deferred.
- I ran the spectral codec at 25 Hz: mel 0.525, 559 codes, probe ceiling 44.4% (the 50 Hz run: 0.463, 630, 40.3%). This supports spec at 25 Hz as the default: half the sequence cost of Route 3's 50 Hz, with no collapse.

4. WHAT MEASURES BADLY, ACROSS ALL ROUTES, SO THE DESIGN SHOWS IT RATHER THAN HIDES IT
- Compositional generalisation is near zero everywhere: 0% understanding on held-out combinations (Route 3), first note 0.0 (Route 2).
- Discrete understanding sits at 45-55% of a dedicated code classifier.
- Codec timbre fidelity is about 0.6.
- Every result is one seed.
Hence EVAL.grounding always splits train and held-out combinations and requires a ground-truth sanity reading of 1.0. The continuous-insert understanding arm (Route 2: 0.978 note accuracy against 0.485 for today's extra= hook) is the first S8 arm.
